  • Recent findings suggest that this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

Recent findings suggest that this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

According to recent reports, “We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

Sources indicate that avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an concern for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

According to recent reports, england thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

A fine team move ended with an excellent Stanway finish. It was her fifth goal in this qualifying campaign and she is England’s top scorer for 2025-26.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman remarked. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

Industry observers note that toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

In a recent development, that opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven major-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

VAR was correct not to overrule Michael Oliver after he awarded a controversial penalty against Morgan Rogers for handball against Leeds, per Dermot Gallagher.

The match was level at 1-1 when Rogers attempted to block a shot from Jayden Bogle. He turned his back in doing so and the ball appeared to catch him on his upper arm, with Oliver immediately pointing to the spot.

VAR reviewed the incident and allowed the penalty to stand, which Dominic Calvert-Lewin duly buried to put Leeds 2-1 up. The match ended 4-1 in the visitors’ favour.

Chelsea fans were left confused by the decision, with many suspecting the ball had caught Rogers above his sleeve and thus did not warrant handball. Rogers, meanwhile, appeared to protest that the ball had hit him in the face.

Xabi Alonso was similarly unimpressed with the decision, saying post-match: “I don’t agree. I think that it was harsh from Michael Oliver. For me it was not a penalty.”.

But, speaking on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch, former Premier League referee Gallagher has opined that VAR was correct to allow Oliver’s decision to stand, pointing out that there was not sufficient evidence to overturn it.

The VAR reviewed a number of different angles of the incident, but none conclusively absolved Rogers.

“You can watch replays, you can watch a multitude of angles, some will say it hit (Rogers) on the elbow and some say the face,” mentioned Gallagher. “There is no conclusive evidence to say the referee is wrong, so he has to give a penalty.

“We are not trying to prove the referee wrong. He gave a penalty. What I am saying is there is no evidence to say the referee is wrong, not that the VAR is gonna say ‘this is the right decision’.

“The referee has given the decision, and the evidence says the referee is not wrong.”.

Jay Bothroyd concurred, admitting he felt that the ball might have hit Rogers too high, but that he would not have liked to see the penalty overturned.

In a recent development, “You have got to stick with the referee's decision,” he declared. “It looked like it hit his sleeve but they have a camera to show the elbow. It is difficult to see.

“When you look at that, (everyone has) an opinion), so you have to stick with the referee's decision.

The 31-year-old has grown into a crucial figure at Arsenal, vital in their Premier League success last season having established himself as the best goalkeeper in the league.

He has missed just one game through injury since joining the Gunners but his withdrawal at St James’ Park sparked huge concern for the champions.

Arsenal boast the strongest squad in the English top flight but former Premier League star Redknapp insists Raya is ‘irreplaceable’, warning Kepa is not of the required standard to come in and replace him.

Redknapp added any absence for Raya could prove extremely costly.

‘Arsenal’s squad, player for player, they have two players for every position,’ Redknapp told Sky Sports.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:50.

Tottenham Hotspur have received a major enhancement on the future of teenage starlet Luca Williams-Barnett.

The highly-rated academy graduate, who turned 18 at the start of October, made a notable impression on his full debut for Spurs in a 2-0 Premier League home win over Ipswich Town last weekend.

Williams-Barnett opened the scoring with his first senior goal in the 15th minute, arriving at the back post to poke the ball home, before a blistering dribble that began from inside his own half helped him to set up Dominic Solanke shortly after half time.

Tottenham’s youngest scorer in the Premier League since Gareth Bale in 2007 received a standing ovation from the home crowd and also picked up the Man of the Match award.

After making his first-team debut as a 16-year-old last season, calls for the skilful winger to get more minutes have only grown louder over a challenging 12 months at Spurs.

Ensuring that Williams-Barnett commits his future to the club has also been high on the agenda, with the youngster having now entered the final 24 months of his current deal.

However, football.london reports that Williams-Barnett has agreed to sign a new long-term deal at Tottenham, seemingly cooling fears that he could leave to join a rival club.

The England Under-19 international has now featured four times in the senior Spurs side under head coach Roberto De Zerbi, who was full of praise for the “special” teenager after the win over Ipswich.

In a recent development, "Luca is a special player,” De Zerbi told reporters post-match. "I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top teammates.

"I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be notable.

Recent findings suggest that "The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom, and Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

"And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

"Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.".

After revealed that Williams-Barnett prepared for the game on the team bus by watching YouTube videos of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, De Zerbi was asked whether the Spurs starlet could reach the same level as Barcelona and Spain sensation Yamal, who finished third in the 2026 Ballon d’Or rankings.

De Zerbi replied: "Yes, I think so, and one of the best things in my career… I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

"I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?".

Williams-Barnett will hope to be rewarded with a second successive start when Tottenham travel to the Stadium of Light to face Sunderland in their next Premier League fixture on Sunday.

The Gunners, who led at the break, were held to a 2-2 draw at St James’ Park as a resilient Newcastle fought their way back into the contest.

While chasing an equaliser, Raya was involved in an innocuous coming together with William Osula in the penalty area.

The Spaniard appeared to be in real pain as he clutched his left arm, using his shirt as a makeshift sling as he left the pitch to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya was visibly distressed and at one stage appeared close to tears as he made his way off, sparking huge concern for the Gunners.

The 31-year-old has grown into a crucial figure at Arsenal, vital in their Premier League success last season having established himself as the best goalkeeper in the league.

Speaking after the draw, Arteta admitted the sight of his shot stopper in pain was ‘not good news’ with Raya to undergo an MRI scan on Sunday.

‘Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news,’ Arteta stated in his post-match press conference.

‘He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don’t know.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 21:00, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 00:04, 22 November 2026.

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I said, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'.

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The chaotic saga of litigation which followed the 2025 AFCON final will finally be resolved this week, as the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) prepares to release its final decision.

The champion of AFCON 2025 remains in dispute after the scandalous events of January 18th, where Senegal were stripped of a 1-0 victory after their squad briefly left the pitch in the second half.

An unprecedented and unsavoury series of events followed. Morocco appealed the result and won, before Senegal escalated the affair to CAS in Lausanne, the world’s premier body for the resolution of sporting disputes.

Now, ten months after the full-time whistle was blown in Rabat, AFCON 2025 will finally have an undisputed champion, though the animosity will surely remain, regardless of the verdict.

Here is everything you need to know about the situation ahead of the final verdict being released...

An official press release from CAS confirms the decision will be released on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

Sources indicate that no specific time of day has been set. The press release simply says the decision will be released “in the course of the afternoon.”.

Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.

Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.

In a recent development, players and staff, led by head coach Pape Thiaw, alike returned to the changing rooms, and the match was paused for 14 minutes. Some Senegal players remained on the pitch and returned to the pitch only at the behest of captain Sadio Mane.

Crucially, the referee never abandoned the match, and play resumed once the entire Senegal squad had returned to the pitch.

Brahim Diaz then missed the vital penalty and Senegal went on to win in extra time, with Villarreal’s Pape Gueye scoring the decider.

In March 2026, two months after the final, CAF announced the shock decision to reverse the result, saying Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch.

The result was thus changed to a 3-0 win for Morocco, who are now considered the AFCON 2025 champions.

The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) immediately hit back at CAF’s decision to strip them of the AFCON title, and have since refused to return the trophy, which they have regularly paraded in public.

Sources indicate that the FSF immediately appealed CAF’s decision and the case fell to CAS. CAF president Patrice Motsepe acknowledged Senegal’s “right” to do so and added that he will “respect the decision that’s taken at the highest level.”.

The government of Senegal has also criticised CAF’s move, expressing “profound dismay” and questioning the governing body’s credibility.

The Moroccan football federation, meanwhile, has called for tournament rules to be “respected” as they maintain their status as champions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Man Utd offered little resistance on Pochettino’s managerial debut at Anfield on Sunday as they were ripped apart 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool following the early dismissal of Leny Yoro.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has already admitted that newly introduced employers Manchester United are in a relegation battle - with some key trends and statistics highlighting why the Red Devils should be genuinely worried about the drop.

Man Utd offered little resistance on Pochettino’s managerial debut at Anfield on Sunday as they were ripped apart 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool following the early dismissal of Leny Yoro.

Fans will have seen that during their own season of constant struggle last term, Tottenham already had 18 points on the board at this stage of the campaign - 10 more than United’s current tally.

Spurs only confirmed their Premier League survival on the final day, edging out rivals West Ham by a single point in a hugely dramatic finish.

There are more alarming numbers and patterns from Premier League history that do not bode well for free-falling United’s fortunes this season.

Over the past 20 years, at least one team in the bottom three after 11 games has gone on to be relegated by the end of the season.

In total, 56.66 per cent of clubs in the relegation zone after 11 matches have finished there.

Pochettino’s side will take solace in the fact that seven teams have previously beaten the drop after picking up exactly eight points from their opening 11 fixtures.

Industry observers note that but that doesn’t tell the full story. Teams with only eight points and sitting in the relegation zone after 11 games have survived on just two previous occasions, with six dropping down to the Championship.

Only Newcastle in 2006/07 and Southampton in 2019/20 beat the drop after starting off with eight points from their first 11 games to languish in the bottom three.

Ipswich sat outside the relegation zone in 2023/24 with eight points from 11 matches, but were unable to stay up come May.

Over the last 20 years, 31 teams with eight points or fewer from their opening 11 fixtures failed to survive; only 24 sides stayed up with that starting tally.

In more concern for United, the other two teams currently in the relegation zone make up six of those latter examples.

Crystal Palace are used to starting slow - twice they have begun the season with four points from 11 games, only to record 11th-place finishes on both occasions.

In total, the Eagles have recovered from eight points or fewer after 11 games to stave off relegation four times, while Sunderland have achieved that feat twice.

What does United’s own history tell us about the current side’s chances of beating the drop?

When United were last relegated from the top-flight, all the way back in 1973/74, the Red Devils had a higher points total after 11 games.

Under the current rules for three points for a win, rather than the two awarded at that time, Tommy Docherty’s side would have had 11 points from their first 11 matches of the 1973/74 First Division season.

In reality they had just nine, after three wins and two draws. Goalkeeper Alex Stepney was their joint-top goalscorer after converting two penalties.

Sources indicate that united finished the season 21st out of 22 teams, five points from safety. Perhaps United fans will take solace from the fact that this season’s start more closely resembles the beginning of the campaign prior to that relegation - five draws, one win and six losses from 12 games.

Industry observers note that in 1972/73, United managed to salvage an 18th-place finish in the old First Division, comfortably beating the drop. Of course, the next season they were relegated for the first time since 1938.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have notified the Football Association (FA) that they intend to appeal Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Man Utd boss at Anfield on Sunday.

Liverpool then romped to an easy 4-0 win, with Pochettino afterwards lamenting referee Sam Barrott’s decision to dismiss Yoro as “unfair”.

The Argentine believed that his player did not deny a goalscoring opportunity, meaning that he should not have seen red.

Yoro clipped the heels of Alexander Isak as the Liverpool attacker bore down on goal, but Pochettino and United fans felt that goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the loose ball before Isak, negating the goalscoring potential.

Under current FA rules, clubs have 14 days to submit an appeal, with United back in action on Saturday as they host Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford.

With his current three-game domestic suspension, Yoro would also miss the trip to Newcastle and visit of Coventry early next month, but remain available for Champions League meetings with Sporting and RB Leipzig.

Yoro’s dismissal on Merseyside was his second in two months, having also received his marching orders in a Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid in October.

Former United boss Michael Carrick questioned that decision at the time and stated his belief that it was not a red card, but no appeal was made by the club.

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:13.

European football returns to the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday evening, when Arsenal welcome a Borussia Dortmund side just one point below them in the Champions League rankings.

The Gunners have navigated their opening four matches unbeaten to collect 10 points and sit third in the table, while Niko Kovac's side have lost one and won three in the continent's top tier so far to lie 12th.

Here, Sports Mole runs through everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund is scheduled for an 8pm kickoff on Tuesday, November 24.

Recent findings suggest that another six matches will commence at the same time, including Manchester City vs. Napoli and Real Madrid vs. PSV Eindhoven.

Arsenal are hosting Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, where Mikel Arteta's men have won each of their first six games in all tournaments this season, conceding just two goals in the process.

BVB last visited Arsenal's home turf in 2014, when Yaya Sanogo and Alexis Sanchez propelled the Gunners to a 2-0 group-stage victory.

It has been revealed that arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund will not be shown on terrestrial television in the UK; instead, the fixture will be broadcast on Amazon Prime Video.

Fans with an Amazon Prime Video subscription can watch the game on a variety of devices, such as via the TV app, phones, computers and games consoles.

Amazon Prime Video costs £8.99 a month for the full Amazon Prime package, or £7.99 a month for just Amazon Prime Video, although the latter is only available to select accounts.

Highlights of the match will be made available on the Amazon Prime and TNT Sports YouTube channels shortly after full time, as well as the official Arsenal account.

The @primevideosport X account will also post short clips of key moments as and when they happen.

It has been revealed that top spot in the Champions League table is within Arsenal's reach, as the third-placed Gunners are just two points behind Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain, the latter of whom do not take to the field until Wednesday vs. Roma.

Arteta's men will therefore rise to first for at least 24 hours if they win and Real Madrid lose to PSV, or if they triumph, Los Blancos draw and Arsenal also make up a -1 goal difference to Jose Mourinho's side.

The Gunners could also equal two Champions League records, as they are a win or draw away from matching their longest-ever run of unbeaten group stage/league phase games (17) and could also draw level with Liverpool's English record of 13 consecutive group stage/league phase wins at home.

On the other hand, Dortmund are capable of rising into the top eight automatic qualification places with a shock win in North London, but head coach Kovac has only won one of his previous five Champions League matches against an English club; a 7-2 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur with Bayern Munich in 2019.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham winger Savio returned from injury on Saturday and almost immediately suffered the same injury that had just kept him out for six weeks.

Spurs beat Ipswich Town 2-0 in north London, thanks to goals from teenager Luca Williams-Barnett on his first Premier League start and Dominic Solanke.

Tottenham climbed to ninth with the win, but there was disappointing news for them as Savio came off the bench in the second half but did not make the final whistle.

The summer-signing from Manchester City had not played since the draw with Manchester United on October 10 and may now face a similar period on the sidelines after a recurrence of the same hamstring problem.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi mentioned: ‘I’m sorry for Savio’s injury, because it was the same injury as last time, and we need him.

‘He’s a crucial player for us. He’s unlucky in this period. We have to be close with him to help him to become the top player we bought at the beginning of this season.’.

The 22-year-old joined from Manchester City for an initial £75 million and scored on his debut in a League Cup win over Charlton Athletic, but has not done much of note since then, hampered by injury.

The emergence of Williams-Barnett is much better news for De Zerbi, who has not been shy in talking up the talents of the 18-year-old who has come through the youth ranks at Spurs.

Sources indicate that ‘Luca is a special player,’ mentioned the Italian. ‘I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He’s lucky because he’s playing in a top club with top team-mates.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my blueprint, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.

‘The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

‘And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

‘Even if they are Ballon d’Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.’.

De Zerbi, who was serving a touchline suspension against Ipswich, was asked if Williams-Barnett could reach the levels of the superstars he mentioned and stated: ‘Yes, I think so.

‘And one of the best things in my career… I’ve seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

‘I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?’.

Spurs have now won four of their last five Premier League games and ended Saturday just three points adrift of Bournemouth in fourth.

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 09:20.

Gameweek five in the Champions League sees Manchester City and Napoli square off in the League Phase.

These two teams suffered contrasting results in the previous round of fixtures, and here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into to their latest encounter.

In a recent development, man City vs. Napoli will kick off at 20:00 UK time on Tuesday night.

This contest is one of nine taking place on the same evening, with Man City’s English rivals Arsenal among those also in action at home to Borussia Dortmund.

This Champions League match will take place at Man City’s home the Etihad Stadium, which now holds a capacity of 61,470 spectators following a recent expansion.

Man City have lost only two of their last 27 home fixtures in the group stage/League Phase of the Champions League (W22 D3), though one of those was earlier this season against holders Paris Saint-Germain (4-2).

In a recent development, man City vs. Napoli will be shown live on TNT Sports 1 or TNT Sports Ultimate for viewers in the UK.

Fans with the TNT Sports package through their TV provider can watch this game on Sky Go and Virgin TV Go, while this fixture will also be streamed live on Amazon Prime Video in the UK, and on CBS on Paramount+ in the USA.

Recent findings suggest that match highlights of Man City vs. Napoli will be available on Amazon Prime Video, TNT Sports and via BBC Sport’s dedicated UEFA Champions League Match of the Day show which you can watch live or stream on BBC iPlayer.

You can also view this match on the TNT Sports YouTube channel and both clubs' official YouTube accounts.

At the halfway stage in the League Phase, Man City sit seventh in the 36-team standings after accumulating nine points from their opening four matches.

Enzo Maresca’s side will realistically need at least a couple more victories to ensure they finish inside the top eight and secure automatic qualification for the last 16, rather than slip into the playoffs.

The Citizens have won each of their last three Champions League meetings with Napoli, most recently winning 2-0 on home soil in the League Phase of last season’s competition courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku.

Napoli will therefore be out for revenge when they make the trip back to the blue side of Manchester, while Wednesday’s fixture also marks the return of City legend Kevin De Bruyne, whose first comeback to the Etihad was cut short.

Indeed, he was the unfortunate one sacrificed after just 21 minutes following a red card for Giovanni Di Lorenzo in Napoli's 2-0 defeat last season.

The Italian club have won one and lost three of their opening four UCL games this term, suffering a disappointing 4-1 defeat at Porto on November 4, and currently sit down in 27th place in the table, six points behind the top eight.

While Napoli enter this contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on Saturday, courtesy of a Scott McTominay goal, Man City were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Fulham in the Premier League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:36.

Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri will reunite with his parent club when Borussia Dortmund take on the Premier League champions in Tuesday's Champions League clash at the Emirates Stadium.

The 19-year-old joined the German giants on a season-long loan during the final hours of the summer transfer window, but he is yet to find his best form under Niko Kovac.

Nwaneri has only provided one assist and no goals from his first 13 appearances in a Dortmund shirt across all competitions, that contribution coming on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim.

Since then, the 2007-born playmaker has only started four Bundesliga matches, and he is still waiting to make a first XI in the Champions League, being restricted to 87 minutes across four substitute outings.

Nwaneri was also given just a one-minute run-out in the weekend's 1-0 Bundesliga win over Borussia Monchengladbach, but he may be given the chance to strut his stuff against his boyhood team.

Sources indicate that champions League rules permit loan players to face their parent clubs in the Champions League, so Nwaneri will be able to feature in Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Unlike in the Premier League and other domestic competitions in England, where loan players cannot take on parent teams without special dispensation, there are no such restrictions outlined in the Champions League rules and regulations.

However, if Nwaneri was to return to Arsenal in January, the England Under-21 international would not be able to feature for the Premier League champions for the remainder of the tournament.

Article 30.05 of UEFA's Champions League regulations states that 'A player may not play in the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League or UEFA Conference League for more than one club in a single season', but Arsenal are not expected to bring Nwaneri back to North London over the winter.

The teenager has scored 10 goals and set up two more in 51 Arsenal games since making his debut against Brentford in September 2022, when he became the Premier League's youngest player of all time.

Recent findings suggest that goal Bayern Munich. Philippe Coutinho. 2-8.

Loan players making decisive contributions against parent clubs in the Champions League has been a semi-regular occurrence, the most notable example being Philippe Coutinho in 2020.

The then-Barcelona playmaker was shipped out to Bayern Munich and reunited with La Blaugrana in the quarter-finals of the 2019-20 edition, when he incredibly scored twice in an 8-2 annihilation.

Sixteen years prior, Fernando Morientes - on loan at Monaco from Real Madrid - scored in both legs of the quarter-final against Los Blancos, helping Les Monegasques knock out his parent team on away goals before they lost to Porto in the final.

Real were also stung by James Rodriguez in the 2017-18 semi-finals vs. Bayern Munich, but the Colombian's goal - which he refused to celebrate - was not enough to prevent Los Blancos advancing 4-3 on aggregate.

The 2013-14 semi-finals saw Thibaut Courtois play a crucial role in Atletico Madrid's success against parent club Chelsea, who tried to force Los Rojiblancos to pay them £2.5m for each game the Belgian goalkeeper played against them, only for UEFA to rule the terms null, void and unenforceable.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Dominik Szoboszlai always knew Florian Wirtz's qualities would eventually shine through for Liverpool after delivering a "world-class" performance against Manchester United.

Wirtz produced one of his most impressive displays since joining the Reds from Bayer Leverkusen last summer in Sunday's 4-0 thrashing of Mauricio Pochettino's side at Anfield.

After Szoboszlai opened the scoring from a free-kick following Leny Yoro's red card, Wirtz doubled Liverpool's lead in the 13th with a superb volley from inside the penalty area.

Liverpool could have pulled further clear, but both Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola wasted presentable opportunities, both of which were teed up by the impressive Wirtz.

Rio Ngumoha got himself on the scoresheet in the 66th minute before Wirtz found Victor Munoz, who took a touch before concluding the rout eight minutes from time.

Wirtz created 10 open-play chances against United, the most by a player in a Premier League match since Manchester City's David Silva against West Brom in March 2015 (11).

He now has eight goal involvements (three goals, five assists) in all competitions in 2026-27, and Szoboszlai believes the Germany international is only just getting started.

Sources indicate that "I always knew he was a good player," Szoboszlai remarked. "He's world-class. I love to play with him. We understand each other very well.

Industry observers note that "I think we are similar types of guys who understand the game in the same way. That's why it's easier for us.

Sources indicate that "Now he's in the flow, scoring against [Crystal] Palace, for the national team and scoring another goal. So yeah, we need him, and he knows that, and he will shine even more.".

Wirtz now ranks either first or joint-first in the Premier League in November for goal involvements (four), expected assists (1.28), chances created (11), defensive line-breaking passes (12), and possession won in the final third (five).

But another fine performance came from the lively Ngumoha, who, aged 18 years and 85 days, became the youngest player to score and assist in a Premier League game for Liverpool since Michael Owen on Boxing Day 1997 (18y 12d v Leeds United).

"Everyone knows how good he is, and he is doing it every week in the games and day by day in the training, because if he wasn't, he may not get the chance," Szoboszlai added.

"So you have to show yourself in the training sessions, show it to the gaffer and then you get the chance. He is doing that every time and, yeah, he is still young with lots to learn.

"The sky is the limit for him. I think his career is like [on an upward trajectory] until now, and now he has to be clever and listen maybe to the older players who have a little bit more experience. Some of us more, some of us less.

"We try to help him, but it's also two parts. He's young, he's 18, so it's a long way to go, and he has to be ready for everything, the ups and downs.

"He cannot be really up when he's up, but also when he's down a little bit, he cannot be really down, so he has to find the balance.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has already instituted a major change at Manchester United in a bid to lift the club’s standards and dodge relegation.

The Argentine’s United tenure got off to a grim start at Anfield on Sunday as Leny Yoro was shown an early red card and Liverpool went on to bag four goals.

The result leaves the club 19th in the Premier League, with the prospect of relegation - or, at the very least, being involved in the relegation battle - more real than ever.

But as Pochettino discovers the true scale of the task at hand, he has wasted little time in imposing his methods on United.

That has begun with scrapping a rule imposed by his predecessor Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the November international break.

While in the job, Carrick had habitually handed the United squad a day off following a match, but Pochettino has promptly done away with that provision.

His players reported to Carrington bright and early on Monday morning for recovery sessions, with a Champions League meeting with Sporting looming on Wednesday evening.

Pochettino has pushed forward their arrival time, too, with some players touching down at the training ground as early as 8.30am.

It has been a busy few days at Carrington. Pochettino has hired a newly introduced strength and conditioning coach to help accommodate his focus on high-pressing football, while the club are also appealing Yoro’s red card.

They are doing so on the basis that Senne Lammens looked set to beat Alexander Isak in his footrace, and, thus, Yoro’s clumsy tackle did not constitute denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

"The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down.

"In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.”.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes a red card for Leny Yoro during Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat by Liverpool was the correct decision - claiming it “would’ve been a surprise” if the defender wasn’t sent off.

Man Utd informed the Football Association (FA) on Monday afternoon of their intention to appeal Yoro’s three-game suspension.

After just eight minutes of Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of United at Anfield, Yoro found himself scrambling to get back after Matthijs de Ligt allowed Alexander Isak through on goal.

Chasing both man and ball, Yoro clipped Isak on the edge of the area - prompting referee Sam Barrott to show a straight red card. At the time Pochettino was spotted aggressively waving his finger, clearly disagreeing with the decision.

But on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch panel, Gallagher couldn’t see any mitigating factors for Yoro.

Sources indicate that he remarked: “If you look at it from the referee's angle, is it a foul? That's the first step. Yeah. Is he in possession of the ball? From that angle, yes.

“I think most people would've expected a red card. It would've been a surprise during the game if a red card hadn't been given.”.

United fans pointed out that goalkeeper Senne Lammens appeared to be reaching the loose ball before Isak, potentially changing the foul from a denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

It has been revealed that asked if he thought that Lammens would have gotten to the ball first, Gallagher replied: "I don't know. You watch it play out. That happens. Do you think it's a red card? Gary Neville's immediate reaction was red card.”.

Industry observers note that gallagher’s fellow pundit, former England striker Jay Bothroyd, was in agreement. "It has to be a red,” he stated.

It has been revealed that “I will say, I'm not sure Isak can get a shot off, but I think he could touch the ball. It's not an obvious goalscoring opportunity, but you don't know. You have to judge if it's a foul, so you have to give the red card.

In a recent development, “Technically, he is in control of the ball because he touched it in that direction. It's if he's heavy or not.".

According to recent reports, "You have to assess where Lammens was. The ball was nearly in his hands.".

There was further frustration for United on Merseyside, with Pochettino believing that his side should have been awarded a penalty in the first half.

Bryan Mbeumo found himself barged off the ball by Jeremy Jacquet inside the box, but the entire panel rejected those claims.

Roy Keane has predicted the biggest threat to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining the Premier League title is unlikely to come from any of their traditional rivals.

The Gunners displayed unfamiliar signs of vulnerability at St James’ Park on Saturday evening where they let a half-time lead slip, before eventually battling back to earn a 2-2 draw.

The loss of two points was compounded by an injury to goalkeeper David Raya who is now nervously anticipating the results of a forthcoming MRI scan on his damaged arm.

Manchester City’s failure to win at home against Fulham meant the failure to cling onto the lead Arsenal gained through Eberechi Eze’s first-half opener represented a missed opportunity.

With Enzo Maresca’s side in the midst of a disappointing run and the likes of Chelsea and Liverpool struggling to come to terms with the demands of their latest managers, Arsenal are widely expected to defend the title they won back in May.

Indeed, their nearest challengers at present are Brighton, who are thriving under the management of Fabian Hurzeler, and Keane sees no reason why the Seagulls can’t continue to mount a challenge.

‘At this moment, yes,’ Keane told Sky Sports when asked if Brighton could emerge as the only team capable of preventing Arsenal from claiming back-to-back titles.

‘That’s because of the form they’re in, they’re goal threat and defensively they’re very, very good.

‘They’ve got a top quality manager but obviously over the next couple of months the pressure and injuries and whatever (will come).

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Sources indicate that ‘They’ve got a young team and have a lack of experience. But at this moment in time they’ve got to enjoy it and keep that pressure on Arsenal.’.

Hurzeler, who masterminded a 3-0 win over the Gunners back in September, has plenty of admirers and was recently linked with the Manchester United job.

‘His time will come,’ Keane stated when it was put to him that the German would’ve represented a better appointment than Mauricio Pochettino.

Sources indicate that ‘We talk about Poch getting close a few times and sliding doors moments. He’s done a great job and Brighton and if he left now you’d be looking at him and thinking he should’ve stuck at it a bit more.

Industry observers note that ‘We talk about loyalty in football and it’s got to work both ways. So I’m glad he continuing at Brighton and hopefully they can continue having a good season.’.

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three substantial guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the major three were on the difference was obvious.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta noted. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. According to recent reports, will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW.

Industry observers note that arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

It has been revealed that as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel).

After signing his upcoming Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

According to recent reports, lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Recent findings suggest that leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

Xabi Alonso could be forgiven for thinking his Chelsea reign is already heading the same way as his recent predecessors following Saturday’s 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Leeds United.

The Spaniard’s appointment in the summer was seen as something of a coup given his exploits at Bayer Leverkusen, allied to the fact Liverpool and Manchester City were both seeking high-profile replacements for their outgoing managers.

A summer of significant investment saw optimism rise at Stamford Bridge and a title challenge was anticipated given the lack of a European football as a distraction.

The honeymoon period is, however, already over for the 44-year-old whose side have lost five times already and are conceding goals, 20 in 11 matches, at an alarming rate.

Despite that unconvincing record, according to Mail Sport, Chelsea will not be making any kneejerk reactions and relieving him of his duties so early in his tenure.

Chelsea have not shied away from making quick decisions on the fates of those they have entrusted with overseeing a rebuilding process in recent years, with both Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior lasting a matter of months at the helm.

Alonso is not yet under the sort of pressure that quickly became too much to handle for Potter and Rosenior, but it is fair to say he is struggling to win over an increasingly frustrated fanbase that voiced its opinion in no uncertain terms on Saturday.

Romeo Lavia, meanwhile, mentioned Chelsea must not give in to panic after they were hammered by one of their bitterest rivals.

The home side were outclassed as Leeds ended a 27-year wait for a Premier League win in west London, with a chorus of boos ringing out at full-time.

‘At home this is never the way you want to finish a game. We let them back in the game when we shouldn’t have. This is something we will analyse and get better at.

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 09:53.

Watford play host to Blackburn Rovers on Wednesday night searching for yet another permanent head coach after the sacking of Alessio Dionisi.

At a time when the Hornets sit in 21st position in the Championship table, Rovers make the trip to Vicarage Road sitting among the mid-table places.

Whenever a new manager arrives at Watford, there is always an inevitability that his stay at Vicarage Road will be a short one.

A 10th defeat across 18 matches in all competitions led to Dionisi being dismissed after Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United.

With Watford having earned four points from games against Lincoln City and Middlesbrough before the international break, it feels that the Italian could have been provided with more time in the dugout.

Instead, the Pozzo Family has decided to act with Watford ending the weekend sitting four points above the relegation zone.

On a positive note, Watford are unbeaten in their last three games at Vicarage Road, collecting seven points in the process, while they have only conceded nine goals in eight home league fixtures during 2026-27.

As for Blackburn, they responded to Tony Mowbray stepping down from his first-team duties with a 2-2 draw at rivals Burnley on Sunday.

Having twice come from behind, Rovers will be satisfied with a deserved share of the spoils at Turf Moor, a result that keeps them 11 points above the relegation zone despite being viewed as one of the favourites for the drop in the summer.

Furthermore, 17 points have been accumulated from their last 10 games, emphasising that they could still challenge for a top-eight spot this campaign.

However, Blackburn remain with just one away win this campaign, only recording seven points from eight matches while shipping 15 goals.

Blackburn Rovers Championship form:.

While the Watford lineup and formation is difficult to predict, personnel changes are expected after the drab performance at Sheffield United.

Hector Kyprianou, Rocco Vata and Luca Kjerrumgaard are all options in midfield and attack.

Three Watford players - Mattie Pollock, Kevin Keben and Martin Payero - are all one yellow card away from a one-match ban.

With Tom Atcheson expected to miss out with the head injury that he sustained at Burnley, Blackburn could switch to a back four.

Jayden Fevrier was introduced as an early substitute at Turf Moor before he was replaced by Ryoya Morishita 62 minutes later, so the latter could get the nod here.

Second-choice goalkeeper Aynsley Pears will remain between the sticks, a consequence of Balasz Toth being ruled out until January with a hand injury.

Watford possible starting lineup:.

Ravaglia; Traore, Coulibaly, Pollock, Keben, Bola; Kayembe, Kyprianou; Vata, Kjerrumgaard, Mavididi.

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:.

Pears; Beyuku, McLoughlin, Carter, Pickering; Montgomery, Baradji; Morishita, Cantwell, Afolayan; Gudjohnsen.

According to recent reports, although both of these teams are without a permanent manager in charge, Blackburn are far more settled than Watford. With that in mind, we are backing the visitors to earn a deserved victory at Vicarage Road, keeping themselves within touching distance of the playoffs in the process.

William Saliba could make his first start of the season for Arsenal against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.

The French defender had a long spell on the sidelines after aggravating a back injury at the World Cup over the summer.

Saliba did not require surgery but a significant spell of rest was needed and he is yet to play a single first-team minute so far this season.

He played the first half for Arsenal’s Under-21s in their PL2 win over Aston Villa before the international break and then featured in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Watford.

Having come through those games without any issues, Saliba is in contention for a first-team return and he could be brought in against Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Goalkeeper David Raya will miss the match with a shoulder injury suffered late on during Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle in the Premier League and deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to start in his place, over Illan Meslier.

Ben White could get the nod at right-back, as he continues to share minutes with Jurrien Timber, while Myles Lewis-Skelly will hope to get his opportunity in midfield.

Arsenal have a huge Premier League match at home to Manchester City to come on Sunday but Bundesliga leaders Dortmund represent tough opposition and manager Mikel Arteta is likely to go strong with his team selection.

That would mean more minutes in midfield for Declan Rice and captain Martin Odegaard, with Martin Zubimendi still sidelined, while Noni Madueke has become an essential part of the attack on the right wing in the absence of Bukayo Saka.

Up front, Viktor Gyokeres' chances to start have largely come in the Champions League this season and it would be no surprise if he was chosen to lead the line against Dortmund, ahead of Kai Havertz.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Feyenoord and Porto meet at De Kuip on Tuesday night with both clubs under pressure to revive their Champions League campaigns.

Recent findings suggest that having collected just three points from their opening four league-phase matches, the Dutch side sit 32nd in the 36-team table, while Porto are only slightly better off in 26th place. With the knockout rounds already beginning to drift out of sight for both teams, victory could prove pivotal.

Feyenoord head into the contest in poor form and desperately searching for a positive result after six matches without a win in all competitions.

It has been revealed that their latest setback came at the weekend when they were beaten 3-2 at home by Excelsior, a result made all the more painful by the fact it marked Excelsior’s first league victory at De Kuip in 46 years. Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side began brightly through an early goal from Givairo Read, but three unanswered goals left Jan Plug’s late strike as little more than a consolation.

The defeat followed a 5-3 loss away to Heerenveen and a 3-0 home defeat to Inter Milan in the Champions League, meaning Feyenoord have conceded at least three goals in each of their last three matches.

Defensive concerns have become a major problem. The Dutch club have now lost 10 of their last 13 European fixtures and have conceded the opening goal in each of their last seven Champions League outings. That sequence includes defeats against Barcelona, Real Betis and Inter Milan, with their only victory in the current campaign coming against Como.

With memories of last season’s disappointing Europa League campaign, when they finished 29th in the league phase, another defeat would leave their hopes of reaching the knockout stages hanging by a thread.

Anis Hadj Moussa is being assessed after returning from international duty with an ankle injury that forced him to miss the defeat against Excelsior.

Tsuyoshi Watanabe is also a doubt after being substituted at half-time on Saturday with a foot problem.

Jakub Moder and Bart Nieuwkoop remain unavailable through injury, while Thomas Beelen, Jordan Bos and Jerry St. Juste are all expected to miss out as well, leaving Van Bronckhorst short of defensive options.

Former Arsenal winger Reiss Nelson made his first start for the club at the weekend, but Luciano Valente could be recalled on the left flank for Tuesday’s encounter.

Porto arrive in Rotterdam with considerably more momentum despite their difficult start to the Champions League campaign.

Francesco Farioli’s side finally claimed their first victory of the league phase on matchday four, producing an emphatic 4-1 win over Napoli. Jan Bednarek, Gabri Veiga, Jakub Kiwior and Samu Omorodion all found the net as the Portuguese side responded impressively after losing their opening three European matches against Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV Eindhoven.

It has been revealed that domestic form has been excellent. Porto have won all 11 of their Primeira Liga matches and already hold a five-point lead at the top of the table. Their most recent outing was less straightforward, though, as they required a penalty shootout to overcome third-tier Paredes in the Taca de Portugal after a 1-1 draw across 120 minutes, due to an extremely unusual own-goal.

The Dragons are competing in the Champions League main stage for the first time in three years and are hoping to reach the knockout rounds for the third consecutive appearance.

According to recent reports, however, their record in the Netherlands offers some encouragement for Feyenoord. Porto have failed to win any of their past four away matches against Dutch opponents, drawing two and losing two. Their previous visits to De Kuip ended in a draw in 1993 and a 2-0 defeat in 2019.

Recent findings suggest that vasco Sousa remains sidelined with a long-term leg injury. Former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling is struggling with a knee problem and is also ineligible, having not been included in Porto’s Champions League squad.

William Gomes has returned to training after recovering from an ankle problem, but his involvement remains uncertain.

Midfielder In-beom Hwang is set for an emotional return against his former club after joining Porto from Feyenoord during the summer, while striker Santiago Gimenez is also returning to Rotterdam after representing Feyenoord between 2022 and 2025.

Feyenoord’s defensive struggles make it difficult to back the hosts with confidence, particularly against a Porto side carrying significantly stronger form and fresh confidence following their dominant victory over Napoli.

While De Kuip remains a challenging venue and Porto’s historical record in the Netherlands is far from convincing, the visitors appear better equipped to handle the pressure of such a crucial European fixture. Given Feyenoord’s recent performances and recurring defensive issues, Porto look capable of taking advantage and securing an vital away victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gary Neville was left ‘absolutely stunned’ by Mauricio Pochettino’s decision to recall Matthijs de Ligt after the defender’s blunder allowed Liverpool to make their breakthrough in a rampant 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

A seemingly innocuous hoiked pass over the top from Liverpool full-back Ronald Araujo wreaked havoc inside United’s half in the tenth minute, leading to Dominik Szoboszlai’s superb opener.

De Ligt had been thrown in for his first appearance of the Premier League season and there were obvious signs of rustiness early on as the Dutchman bizarrely let Araujo’s hopeful ball run through to Alexander Isak.

Isak’s eyes will have lit up as he raced in behind in acres of space and United were guilty of yet more calamitous defending just moments later as Leny Yoro clattered into the back of the Liverpool striker on the edge of the penalty area.

Referee Samuel Barrott wasted little time in showing Yoro a straight red card for the clumsy foul, reducing the visitors to ten men in a nightmare start to Pochettino’s reign as manager.

United’s woes were soon compounded as Szoboszlai struck the resulting free-kick emphatically beyond a despairing Senne Lammes to break the deadlock and send the Anfield crowd into raptures.

Liverpool were not done there, though, and it was Florian Wirtz who directed home Rio Ngumoha’s cross with an audacious flicked finish to double the hosts’ advantage inside only 13 minutes.

A pair of well-taken goals from Ngumoha and Victor Munoz further increased the deficit in a dominant second half for Andoni Iraola’s men, who finished the weekend three points clear of Bournemouth in fourth place.

When watching back replays of the catalogue of errors leading to Liverpool’s opener, former United full-back Neville revealed just how ‘stunned’ he had been left by the decision to select De Ligt in the first place.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘When I saw Matthijs de Ligt’s name on the teamsheet, I have to be honest with you, I was absolutely stunned,’ Neville said on Sky Sports’ commentary of the match.

‘The reason I was stunned was because of this: if you watched him against Como four weeks ago, he was very much well of it.

According to recent reports, ‘That is just a basic ball over the top of him. It’s his problem to start with.’.

Though De Ligt was the main focus of Neville’s criticism, Yoro did not escape without receiving some barbs of his own.

‘Leny Yoro can be further across but if you look at De Ligt in this channel, he’s miles away from him,’ Neville added.

‘Yoro should be across, yes, he can get further around. He has to cover and he doesn’t. He reacts late, his anticipation is really poor.

‘And because he doesn’t play the ball, Yoro, it could be outside the box but it is a red card.

‘It’s so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these kinds of mistakes.’.

According to Neville, Yoro had displayed great ‘naivety’ in getting himself sent off so early in the Premier League contest.

‘He’s not happy with it, Mauricio Pochettino,’ the ex-England international continued.

‘You could argue with it, Isak just delays slightly to make sure that Yoro runs into the back of him.

‘But unfortunately, when you’re a young defender, you’re going to get caught like that and it’s naivety.’.

Switching his focus back to De Ligt, Neville said the Netherlands international had likely been ‘exposed’ as a result of playing so little football over the last 12 months.

‘We saw it against Como and he’s been out for a year, trying to come back to this level of football. It’s really tough,’ he went on.

‘To have De Ligt out there in a game like this, in a back four, he’s been exposed inside the first ten minutes.

‘I have to say, Yoro’s positioning covering is really poor. It’s poor.

‘Yoro has got to be across and around the other centre-back. You’ve got to cover your mate and he doesn’t. It’s really just bad all round from Manchester United.

‘Michael Carrick will be watching this at home and thinking, “Yeah, that’s what I was having to deal with two weeks ago”, it’s so poor.’.

Neville’s Sky Sports’ colleague Jamie Carragher was similarly unimpressed by United’s defending, branding the visitors’ start ‘absolutely shocking’.

‘It’s as bad as it gets from two centre-backs,’ the former Liverpool and England defender mentioned.

‘The ball from Ronald Araujo… it wasn’t even a pass, it’s just a clearance, a hopeful ball through the middle.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

It has been revealed that an extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

According to recent reports, such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

Sources indicate that we could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

According to recent reports, cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

Industry observers note that we wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

According to recent reports, leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole demonstrated up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Industry observers note that palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Recent findings suggest that colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

According to recent reports, the tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him.

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Industry observers note that then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

In a recent development, but the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are at the moment in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal.

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.
