💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino stated Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.
  • Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.
  • The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino stated Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.

The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

Isak’s touch was heavy and United goalkeeper Senne Lammens promptly retrieved the ball but referee Samuel Barrott still deemed a red card to be the suitable punishment.

To make matters worse for Manchester United, Dominik Szoboszlai blasted home the subsequent free-kick to put the hosts ahead.

Liverpool scored again just five minutes later – Florian Wirtz volleying home a cross from the lively Rio Ngumoha.

England winger Ngumoha, 18, scored Liverpool’s third 20 minutes into the second half before Víctor Munoz added a fourth late on.

Pochettino described his first match as Manchester United manager as ‘painful and disappointing’ but criticised the early red card that paved the way for the heavy defeat.

‘So painful. So disappointed,’ Pochettino mentioned in his post-match interview. ‘It’s not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it’s so painful.

‘The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to the calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality.

Sources indicate that leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

It has been revealed that ‘We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field. We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.’.

In a recent development, pochettino, who was hired as Michael Carrick’s replacement last week, added: ‘The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

‘When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper; he runs and goes down.

‘In Leny’s case, it wasn’t intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

It has been revealed that ‘If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty.

‘How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility; I take the responsibility. We keep pushing.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most crucial. At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel.

‘That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card.’.

Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone prior to the November international break, when Carrick was relieved of his duties.

Results over the weekend leave the Red Devils second from bottom in the Premier League with just eight points from their first 11 games of the campaign.

Liverpool, meanwhile, climb back into the Champions League places after an emphatic win over United.

Anfield boss Andoni Iraola noted: ‘We have been very good away this season but at home we haven’t been good enough and still haven’t been good enough.

‘We needed a significant game, and Manchester United is always a big game, to finish like this.

‘It’s true the game’s condition changes because they play with 10 most of the game, but still we’ve done our job, we controlled the game and I think it’s always nice when you can win like this in these kind of games.’.

Asked for his take on the early red card, Iraola added: ‘I think he’s the last man, no? It’s a clear foul and a red card, yes?’.

Manchester United and Liverpool both return to Champions League action this week, with the former travelling to Sporting and the latter visiting Club Brugge.

Luca Williams-Barnett revealed that Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi played a prank on the teenager ahead of his maiden Premier League goal for the club.

The 18-year-old grabbed the opener against Ipswich Town at the weekend, before going on to mark his first full Premier League start with an assist for Dominic Solanke.

The winger had been involved in the first-team squad for the last four Premier League games prior to the Ipswich match, and had continued to train with De Zerbi’s squad in the week.

As such, being told that he was playing for the Under-21s would have been a shock for the young star.

He revealed De Zerbi’s practical joke in an interview with SpursPlay: "The day before, the gaffer obviously pulled me aside.

In a recent development, "He actually said, ‘You’re going to be playing with the ‘21s, 60 minutes to get your legs back,’ and I was like, ‘What?’ but obviously he told me the news and the whole day I was just buzzing. I couldn’t wait.

"Everything I’ve dreamed of. Obviously scoring and getting an assist, it’s like a dream come true basically.".

Williams-Barnett admitted he thought he had spurned his chance for a dream debut, missing a similar opportunity to the move that led to his goal.

He said: “The first ball into the box I wasn’t really there and I was quite annoyed because it was open and I could have had the goal.

“Once I saw it go back to Pedro [Porro], it was an instinct. Once I saw he was able to cross the ball, I just had to get behind my man and put the ball in the goal.”.

Andoni Iraola was keen to play down Liverpool’s Premier League title hoeps in the wake of his side’s 4-0 win over Manchester United.

The rampant Reds ensured it was a miserable day for upcoming Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino, who saw his side 2-0 down and reduced to 10 men after just 13 minute.

In truth, the margin of victory could have been much greater were it not for some wasteful finishing, but second half strikes from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the gloss on an emphatic victory.

With Arsenal having dropped points at Newcastle on Saturday, Liverpool have reduced the gap at the top to seven points and recovered some ground following their defeat to the champions at Anfield nearly a month ago.

Asked, after the first landmark victory of his tenure, whether Liverpool were in the title race, however, Pochettino was keen to play down expectations.

‘It’s still early days,’ Iraola told Sky Sports. ‘I think we are missing the two significant games we lost here at home between Arsenal and [Manchester City] they are making the difference in the standings.

It has been revealed that ‘This is still so early. This doesn’t stop because we have a very difficult game against Borussia Dortmund and then we have the big derby.’.

There was no getting away, though, from the chasm that exists between the two north west heavyweights and Iraola was thrilled with what his burgeoning team delivered in front of their own fans.

Florian Wirtz and Ngumoha were particularly to the fore and the Spaniard was keen to praise two key members of his attacking cohort.

On the apparently rejuvenated Wirtz, he added: ‘He’s in a lovely moment and we want to keep him there as much as we can.

‘He’s in a situation against 10 players where you need players like him to control the situation and see the passes in behind.

‘He’s also arriving more and not just scoring but being a threat. He’s becoming another option and I’m happy with him.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Florian Wirtz was quick to shut down any suggestion that Liverpool were spending too much time ‘thinking about’ Arsenal after their 4-0 win over Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start in what was ultimately a mismatch between the two bitter rivals, with the Red Devils proving their own worst enemy and giving themselves a mountain to climb early on at Anfield.

Some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s tenth-minute breakthrough and saw the latter shown a straight red card by referee Samuel Barrott, a decision that only compounded the visitors’ woes.

The impressive Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later to send the home crowd into raptures, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz completed the rout.

Having cut a frustrated figure on the touchline for the most part, Pochettino made it clear he was less than impressed by the officiating on show as he faced the media shortly after the final whistle on Merseyside.

The Argentinian will no doubt be desperate to turn the tide when United return to Premier League action at home to Brentford in six days’ time, following a midweek trip to Sporting.

The result ensured Pochettino’s men finished the weekend just one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace, with the Old Trafford giants now leading Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Liverpool, meanwhile, moved four points clear of fifth-placed Bournemouth and just one point behind Arsenal’s two nearest rivals, Manchester City and Brighton, after ten games.

‘Really good. The atmosphere after the game was so good. We could enjoy it and it was just a nice afternoon,’ Wirtz – named man of the match – said of the victory in his post-match interview with Sky Sports.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I feel very good but it’s also because the team develops and gets better.

‘Just being part of this, you also get better, so I’m just enjoying that.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Asked if he was perhaps benefitting from being coached by Andoni Iraola and Jurgen Klopp at club and international level, Wirtz replied: ‘Both are very good coaches and I enjoy playing under both.

‘They both bring different qualities and I’m just happy and can be happy to have two of these coaches.’.

Victory in next Sunday’s Merseyside derby at Everton would see Liverpool move to within four points of Arsenal, who host Manchester City later that same afternoon.

When asked if the 4-0 thumping of United had taken Liverpool to ‘another level’, Wirtz replied: ‘Yeah, it was definitely crucial today, also for the table situation.

‘I think a lot of teams on top of the table, they didn’t win this weekend so it’s good that we could use the chance.

‘The red card influenced the game a bit of course but we take that, we earned it because of the run of Alex [Isak] so yeah, very good.’.

Wirtz was then asked if he was ‘thinking about’ Arsenal and possibility of winning the league this season, and his answer was unequivocal.

It came after the Gunners – the reigning Premier League champions – surrendered a first-half lead to drop points away to Newcastle.

‘Uh, I wasn’t talking about Arsenal… all the teams, I don’t know, from one to three,’ Wirtz responded.

‘So we knew, we didn’t speak so much about it, but I think everybody knew it was a big chance to make some points.

‘I’m happy we used this chance.’.

Jamie Carragher says he ‘felt sorry’ for Matthijs de Ligt during Manchester United’s Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Ten-man United were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Old Trafford manager.

The visitors were reduced to ten men inside ten minutes as Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

If that early blow was not bad enough, Liverpool took the lead from the subsequent free-kick as Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home yet another set-piece goal.

Manchester United were fearing an embarrassing battering when Florian Wirtz put Liverpool two goals ahead on 13 minutes with a neat finish from Rio Ngumoha’s cross.

England international Ngumoha, 18, turned provider to goalscorer in the second-half before Victor Munoz added Liverpool’s fourth late on.

Carragher was particularly critical of De Ligt after the match but mentioned he ‘felt sorry’ for the Manchester United centre-back who made his first start of the season at Anfield.

‘I thought it was a really strange decision,’ Carragher mentioned on Sky Sports when asked about Pochettino’s decision to start De Ligt. ‘It was such a bizarre decision.

‘Not because of his quality because I think he’s a better centre-back than Harry Maguire when you look at what he’s achieved in his career and the clubs he’s played for.

‘He’s played for some top football clubs – Bayern Munich, Ajax and Juventus – those are some of the biggest clubs in the world.

Yet another deflating result leaves Manchester United 19th in the Premier League with just eight points from 11 games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United turn their attention back to the Champions League on Wednesday night when they travel to the Estadio Jose Alvalade to face Sporting Lisbon.

Recent findings suggest that the visitors arrive in Portugal reeling from another damaging Premier League defeat, while Sporting are in a much healthier position as they continue their pursuit of a place in the Champions League knockout rounds. At the halfway stage of the league phase, Sporting sit 10th in the 36-team standings, seven places and three points above United.

Sporting have made a solid start to their Champions League campaign and remain firmly in the hunt for automatic qualification.

According to recent reports, the Portuguese side have taken nine points from their opening four league-phase matches, recording victories over Galatasaray, Lens and Shakhtar Donetsk. Their only setback came in a disappointing 3-2 home defeat against LASK Linz on matchday three.

Recent findings suggest that their most recent European outing saw them edge past Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0, and Sporting now head into this fixture under the guidance of new head coach Paulo Fonseca, who has enjoyed a positive start since replacing Rui Borges earlier this month. Sporting have won both matches under his leadership so far.

Sources indicate that before the international break, the Lions claimed a narrow 1-0 Primeira Liga victory over Moreirense, before a heavily rotated side eased to a 4-0 win over fourth-tier Uniao da Serra in the Taca de Portugal on Saturday. Despite those positive results, Sporting remain nine points behind league leaders Porto domestically.

According to recent reports, one statistic will particularly encourage the hosts ahead of Wednesday’s clash. Sporting have scored in each of their last 22 Champions League group-stage or league-phase matches, the longest such run by a Portuguese club.

Sporting are hopeful of welcoming back Zeno Debast and Nuno Santos, both of whom are recovering from muscle injuries, although their involvement remains uncertain.

According to recent reports, fonseca is expected to restore several key players to the starting lineup, including Goncalo Inacio, Ivan Fresneda, Issa Doumbia, Rodrigo Zalazar and Geny Catamo. Chelsea loanee Jesse Derry is also pushing for a place in the side.

Colombian striker Luis Suarez is expected to return after being rested at the weekend. He has scored 13 goals in 15 appearances this season, including four in four Champions League matches.

Manchester United make the trip to Portugal searching for a response after a disastrous start to the Mauricio Pochettino era.

The Argentine watched his side suffer a humiliating 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with United reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro’s controversial early red card. The defeat left the Red Devils 19th in the Premier League table with just eight points, their lowest tally after 11 matches since the 1972-73 season.

Pochettino has publicly acknowledged that the club is involved in a relegation battle and now faces the challenge of tightening a defence that has conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season, more than any other club in Europe’s top five leagues.

According to recent reports, european form has been inconsistent for United. They have beaten Sabah and Roma but suffered defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como. The victory over Roma was particularly dramatic, with the Red Devils coming back from two goals down to win 3-2.

It has been revealed that united’s away record in the Champions League offers little encouragement. They have won only one of their last 11 away matches in the competition, a 2-0 victory at Villarreal in 2021-22.

In a recent development, there is at least some comfort in the head-to-head record. United have won three of their previous four meetings with Sporting, including both group-stage clashes during their successful 2007-08 Champions League campaign.

Sources indicate that united remain without injured trio Manuel Ugarte, Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko. There are also doubts over Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw and reserve goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

The visitors will definitely be without Matheus Cunha, who is suspended after being sent off in the previous Champions League fixture despite scoring the winning goals against Roma.

Matthijs de Ligt endured a difficult outing against Liverpool and could make way for Harry Maguire, with Pochettino expected to retain a three-man defence alongside Leny Yoro and Lisandro Martinez.

In attack, the absence of Cunha could open the door for either Amad Diallo or Joshua Zirkzee, while captain Bruno Fernandes is set to face Sporting for the first time since leaving the club in January 2020. Fernandes scored 64 goals in 137 appearances for Sporting and has contributed 21 goals in 29 Champions League matches during his career.

Sporting enter the match with greater stability, better form and significantly stronger defensive foundations than their visitors. Fonseca has made a positive start in Lisbon, while the hosts continue to score regularly both domestically and in Europe.

Manchester United are desperately in need of a morale-boosting result, but their defensive concerns have shown little sign of improvement and they now face one of the most consistent attacking sides in Portugal. With Sporting boasting strong Champions League form and United struggling badly away from home, the hosts appear well positioned to collect another important three points.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The UK was the sole bidder to host the tournament, and received a 4.3 out of 5 rating from FIFA evaluators.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup will be hosted jointly by England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, FIFA have confirmed, with the tournament returning to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966.

The UK was the sole bidder to host the tournament, and received a 4.3 out of 5 rating from FIFA evaluators.

Recent findings suggest that the bid has put forward 19 potential venues, including five in London: Wembley Stadium, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Emirates, Stamford Bridge and a renovated Selhurst Park. Old Trafford will be considered, regardless of whether Manchester United moves to its proposed new home.

Recent findings suggest that some 32 teams will contest the 2027 World Cup in Brazil, but this is due to expand to 48 from 2031 onwards. The tournament, then, will comprise 104 matches.

England has not hosted a major tournament since staging the women’s European Championships in 2022, which the Lionesses won. It has failed in bids to host the 2006 and 2018 men’s World Cups. England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the Men’s European Championship in 2028.

Industry observers note that it is understood that the process of finalising the list of stadia that will be used is ongoing and is under FIFA’s jurisdiction. Wembley is the only stadium that currently meets the standards required to host the World Cup final.

Burnham calls for ambition after ‘deeply disappointing’ Cop31 disagreements.

South East Water slumps to loss after hefty bill from supply failures.

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean.

It is still to be decided how many of the co-host nations will qualify automatically for the tournament.

The 2035 World Cup bid has also put forward a host stadium in Northern Ireland - Belfast’s Windsor Park - and two each in Scotland and Wales. The Scottish grounds are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road, while the Welsh pair are both in Cardiff: the Millennium Stadium and the Cardiff City Stadium.

The remaining English host stadiums are: Villa Park, The AmEx, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, and the Stadium of Light.

Three more stadia could be added to the bid, most notably a potential upcoming Chelsea ground. Discussions as to the future of Stamford Bridge have been bubbling away for decades as the club’s hierarchy debate whether to redevelop the current ground, knock it down to build a new one on the current site, or move to a new site altogether.

Birmingham City’s latest Powerhouse Stadium and Wrexham’s renovated Racecourse Ground could also host matches.

Sources indicate that prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed the news, saying: “The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

In a recent development, “Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.”.

FA CEO Mark Bullingham remarked: “Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.”.

England last hosted a World Cup in 1966, when the men’s team famously beat West Germany 4-2 in the final to seal the nation’s first major honour. The Lionesses have since become back-to-back Euros champions in 2022 and 2025, but suffered World Cup final heartbreak in 2023 when they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in Sydney.

Before the UK’s host bid for 2035 was confirmed at a special FIFA Congress, it was also revealed that a joint bid by the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica had been approved to host the 2031 World Cup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:10.

Stoke City square off against Millwall on Wednesday night looking for the win that would keep the club in the automatic promotion spots of the Championship table.

At a time when the Potters are in second position, Alex Neil visits one of his former club with the Lions beginning the week in 16th place.

The November international break came at the wrong time for Stoke, who have established themselves as contenders for promotion to the Premier League.

Nevertheless, Mark Robins's side returned on Saturday with a 1-0 win over then-leaders Birmingham City, making it 10 victories from their last 13 games in the Championship.

Rather incredibly, Stoke have accumulated 16 points from their last six games without scoring more than twice in a single match.

Just two goals have been conceded during that period, while Stoke have four clean sheets from their most recent six games at the bet365 Stadium, including their last three.

Despite starting the campaign with three successive defeats, no team in the Championship has won more games (10) than Stoke in 2026-27.

Meanwhile, Neil takes his players to one of his former employers with Millwall having lost five of their most recent seven games.

Three successive defeats, the latest being a 1-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers, have essentially left the Scot fighting to keep his job at The Den.

Millwall, who reached the playoffs last season, are nine points adrift of eighth spot, and defeat to Stoke would leave the East London outfit cut adrift from the mid-table places.

As well as losing five of their eight away matches this campaign, Millwall have conceded 18 goals on their travels, the joint-second worst defensive record in such fixtures in the division.

Stoke could make at least three changes, a consequence of Luca Bombino's red card against Birmingham and Djibril Soumare and George Hirst both picking up injuries in the same game.

Eric-Junior Bocat should start at left wing-back, Svante Ingelsson is in line to feature in midfield should Ethan Galbraith not return after illness, and Sam Gallagher could get the nod ahead of Robert Bozenik in attack.

Million Manhoef may also start on one of the flanks should Robins wish to introduce further fresh legs.

Meanwhile, Alfie Doughty could be introduced as a straight replacement for suspended Millwall defender Zak Sturge.

When the Lions have failed to score in three successive matches, Zak Lovelace and Mihailo Ivanovic will also feel in contention to start in the final third.

Luke Cundle, Romain Esse and Josh Coburn will all be assessed after missing the QPR defeat on Saturday.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Ingelsson, McGlynn, Bocat; Devenny, Gallagher, Bae.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lovelace; Ivanovic.

It has been revealed that while this contest could prove to be closer than many are anticipating, it is difficult to back against a Stoke side that are showing many battling qualities to stay in their current position. With that in mind, we are predicting a narrow win for the Potters.

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed fresh deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but new manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United.

'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always revealed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

It has been revealed that 'And I've always noted the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club says "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a fresh contract so I think that from their side indicates that they want me to stay.

In a recent development, 'As I said there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most vital thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'.

Industry observers note that the club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a substantial-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

In a recent development, united right now sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he claims in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he mentioned.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'.

Recent findings suggest that his post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he said. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference.

Sources indicate that 'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

It has been revealed that 'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

Sources indicate that 'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

In a recent development, 'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'.

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he released a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very promptly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

It has been revealed that ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn.

It has been revealed that they certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Recent findings suggest that ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a substantial game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Sources indicate that martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

Industry observers note that it now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

Industry observers note that but domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

Recent findings suggest that they seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Industry observers note that atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

The one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peter Schmeichel believes simply avoiding relegation should be Mauricio Pochettino’s main ‘target’ at Manchester United this season.

Pochettino took charge of United for the first time away to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon and it proved a nightmare start for the Argentine, with his side thumped 4-0 at Anfield.

The Red Devils were reduced to ten men in only the tenth minute after Leny Yoro brought down Alexander Isak, and the visitors’ woes were compounded as Dominik Szoboszlai scored with the resulting free-kick.

Man-of-the-match Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the hosts out of sight.

The result ensured United remained firmly in the relegation zone at the end of the weekend’s drama, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

The Old Trafford giants, who now lead Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions), will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters at Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

‘Realistically, can Manchester United just finish tenth or 12th? It would be okay,’ former United goalkeeper Schmeichel said on Viaplay following the side’s heavy defeat on Merseyside.

‘I know it’s silly to say but we are in the relegation zone and this team looks like a team that could get relegated.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Recent findings suggest that ‘So now that should be the target. Weirdly enough, at the moment it looks like it [that avoiding relegation is the target].

‘But we [Viaplay’s punditry panel] have all played in the Premier League so we know we’re in November, we’re approaching December, it’s not really now.

‘It’s when we get to March and if they keep doing this for so long, I mean there’s going to be trouble.

‘But I think, at least I have faith that he [Pochettino] can correct those things.

‘He’s never going to make them a championship winning team, not these guys.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It was some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro that led to Liverpool’s breakthrough against United, with the latter guilty of fouling Alexander Isak after failing to cover his centre-back partner.

And while it was De Ligt that made the initial mistake, Yoro was the main focus of Schmeichel’s post-match criticism.

‘I think Isak is doing really well,’ the Dane remarked when watching back replays of the move.

‘When Yoro comes in, Isak cuts across him and yes, he brings him down.

‘It’s terrible defending, it is. Not for that on its own but why is he not reading the ball over the top, over De Ligt?

‘Yoro should have been supporting his co-defender and he’s not.’.

Schmeichel has long been an outspoken critic of Lisandro Martinez and branded the defender ‘disgraceful’ in the wake of United’s 2-0 loss to Chelsea last month.

It came just a fortnight after Martinez had introduced an explosive attack on United’s board, in which he suggested the squad had been repeatedly let down by the club’s recruitment team.

‘I’m fed up talking about him. Honestly, I’m fed up talking about him,’ Schmeichel said of Martinez following United’s latest setback.

‘He’s a guy that criticises people upstairs, criticises his team-mates… I think you have to perform better than that, I really do think that.

‘You can through not all of the goals, but you can go through a couple of the goals and he’s there, at the centre of that, and he could have done something to at least make it harder for Liverpool to score.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto De Zerbi accused former club Marseille of using him as a "scapegoat" despite him giving "everything" for them.

De Zerbi took charge of Marseille in June 2024 on a three-year contract and led them to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 in his debut campaign.

He also came within seconds of winning the Trophee des Champions in the following campaign, but Goncalo Ramos scored a 95th-minute equaliser for Paris Saint-Germain to take the game to penalties, and Marseille lost the shootout.

De Zerbi's tenure did not last much longer after that; a Champions League league-phase exit was followed by a 5-0 Classique hammering, which resulted in his departure in February.

The Italian was not out of a job for long, signing with Tottenham at the end of March, but he has now hit out at Marseille for what he feels was unjust treatment.

"Many times, I was the scapegoat for everyone, but in such an crucial club and city, everyone has to take responsibility, not just a few people, of whom I was one," De Zerbi told Canal+, as quoted by TNT Sports.

"I'm sorry, because when I signed for Marseille, I wanted it so badly and I thought I would stay for many years.

"However, some people didn't keep their word to me. They told me things they didn't follow through on. A year and a half had passed before the Champions Trophy in Kuwait.

"We were on the verge of winning a title after a 12-year drought. Since that match, the situation deteriorated; it worsened until my departure.

According to recent reports, "Marseille is one of the clubs I hold closest to my heart, along with Foggia. I suffered a lot when I left. I suffered because I gave everything in Marseille.".

Moving forward as one https://t.co/NSYHCeV5Wp.

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 21, 2026.

De Zerbi has impressed since arriving at Spurs, ensuring they kept their Premier League status on the last day of the 2025-26 season.

Though they failed to win their first six Premier League games this term, they have since lost just one of their last five (W4) to move them up to ninth in the table.

However, he has admitted he does not see himself remaining in coaching for a long time, as he is keen to explore life outside of football, though he is in no hurry to leave the dugout just yet.

"I don't think I'll stay in football much longer. Your life revolves around football, but life isn't just that," he added.

"That time hasn't come yet. For me, being a coach at this level is already a dream.

Sources indicate that "I don't measure dreams by the titles won, but more by the human impact you have. I always want to stay the same and always look people in the eye. Even when I make mistakes, because I make a lot of them.".

Francesco Pio Esposito was in sensational form on Sunday, scoring a hat-trick in Inter Milan's 4-4 draw with Atalanta BC in Serie A.

The 21-year-old has now netted seven times and registered two assists in 14 appearances for Inter during the 2026-27 campaign, and there is right now a host of speculation surrounding his future at San Siro.

Manchester United allegedly recently scouted the 6ft 3in striker, with the Red Devils planning to bring in a fresh forward next year.

Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with Esposito, who has 18 goals and nine assists in 64 appearances for Inter in all competitions.

As expected, the form of the Italy international against Atalanta drew huge praise from the Italian media.

What did the Italian media say about Esposito performance?

Corriere dello Sport handed Esposito an overall performance rating of 8/10 and branded the striker "unstoppable" for his excellent display.

Tuttosport called the striker "Super Pio" and focused on his contribution to Inter's attacking display, but it was still not enough to secure his side all three points.

Tuttomercatoweb said "Esposito like Haaland" during their post-match piece, with the Inter forward being compared to Manchester City and Norway striker Erling Haaland.

Meanwhile, Sky Sport Italia gave him Inter's highest rating of 8/10.

Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems are expected to put Man United in the market for a upcoming striker in January, but they might have to wait until the end of the campaign to bring in a massive-name player in that area of the field.

Inter are mentioned to value Esposito in the region of £84m, but that could prove to be a bargain if he continues to develop throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

Esposito has scored 10 times in 15 appearances for Italy, and he seemingly has the skill set to be a huge success in the Premier League.

Man United may bring in an experienced option, most likely on loan, during the January market, before launching a significant-money move for Esposito next summer, providing that they are able to hold off the threat of Premier League relegation.

Did ex-Arsenal star Nicolas Pepe really need eye surgery after staring at solar eclipse?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.
  • Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.
  • A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, showed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, showed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

It has been revealed that ‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour quickly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’.

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since joining Villarreal from Trabzonspor back in 2024, Pepe has made a total of 86 appearances for the Spanish club, chipping in with 14 goals and 18 assists in that time.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss sprung a surprise with his inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in his starting XI at Anfield, with the Dutchman having been sidelined for over a year with a persistent back injury.

It remains to be seen whether he will play again here, with Harry Maguire introduced in the first half and shoring up United’s back five.

The England international should start here, perhaps alongisde Yoro, who will not be suspended for this match with his ban only for league games.

That could see Lisandro Martinez plugged at left-back once more, although the Argentine had to shift back inside after Yoro’s red card, with Dorgu shifting back to wing-back from his left wing berth.

Diogo Dalot failed to truly impress on Merseyside and could see himself rotated for Noussair Mazraoui, while in the engine room, Youri Tielemans was hooked for Mason Mount in the second half.

Bryan Mbeumo was the man sacrificed following the sending-off as Pochettino resorted to damage limitation, but the Cameroon international should get the nod here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he remarked, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

In a recent development, 🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk.

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’.

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

It has been revealed that ‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he said. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

According to recent reports, ‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

It has been revealed that ‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

He added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’.

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

While playing the entire match at a numerical disadvantage certainly played a role in the one-sided nature of such an eagerly anticipated contest, United were second best from the off and were made to pay for their latest manager’s questionable team selection.

The decision to drop Harry Maguire at the expense of Matthijs de Ligt, who is still feeling his way back from a long-term injury, was questioned by the likes of Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville before kick-off and their skepticism was vindicated when the Dutch centre-half played a role in Yoro’s red card.

Gerrard, meanwhile, went a step further in his criticism by accusing Pochettino of showing a lack of respect to Maguire by relegating him to the bench in his first game at the helm.

‘I thought he got it wrong,’ Gerrard told The Overlap. ‘I thought he got it wrong in the back line. I think to start someone in a game of that magnitude, it’s the biggest game in the country. All eyes are on it all over the world.

It has been revealed that ‘To play someone that hadn’t played since last November. You can understand the manager wanting to come in and put his stamp on it and change a few things that had been going on previously, but Harry Maguire’s their best defender at the moment.

‘Forget the youngsters that are maybe not ready at the moment. Matthijs de Ligt’s been out for a year. Harry Maguire’s their best defender at the moment. He should have started the game.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He’s one who is rolling his sleeves up and having a go. Okay, he hasn’t been perfect, but to not play him and put de Ligt in before him, I thought it was a bit disrespectful.’.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was important that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Sources indicate that frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

It has been revealed that however, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

In a recent development, the frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

Sources indicate that frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

Just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

It has been revealed that the two-goal lead was very swiftly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

In a recent development, in the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

It was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

Sources indicate that amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

Industry observers note that the change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

Not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

There was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

Continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for firm, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

Milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

According to recent reports, with 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

Sources indicate that pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

Sources indicate that milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.

De Bruyne returns to the Etihad Stadium for the second straight season for another Champions League encounter, but the Belgian has been the subject of speculation.

It has been reported that the 35-year-old, who only joined the Serie A giants from Man City last summer, could be on his way out as early as the January transfer window.

PSV has been touted as a possible destination for De Bruyne, with the midfielder out of contract at the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

De Bruyne's wife revealed in a recent magazine interview that she would one day like to return to Belgium, though De Bruyne said her words were misinterpreted by the Italian media and was keen to put the record straight.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm quite sorry about it all, to be honest. If you go and read the article which you have not read, you will understand what she said," De Bruyne told reporters.

"I was away in Belgium and then a lot of things were being said and there were a lot of negative reactions towards my wife.

"I saw photos of my house in the press, which is not good. I know that journalists in Italy have created this situation and I don't know why.

"You do not know my private life, you have no right to comment on my private life. It was an unpleasant situation for me and my wife.".

When pressed further on his future in Naples, De Bruyne added: "I can't say very much at this point. I've played at 400% so far.

"I'm not 20 years old anymore, I'm almost 36, so there are lots of things to consider.

"Right now, there's not a lot to say. I'm playing well, I'm trying to help the team to do well. There have been lots of challenges this year and a lot of things have happened.".

Mauricio Pochettino’s priority in the January transfer window will not centre on strengthening Manchester United’s leaky defence.

After Sunday’s 4-0 drubbing at the hands of Liverpool, the Red Devils now possess the most porous rearguard in any of Europe’s top five leagues.

Michael Carrick’s successor was given an instant reality check at Anfield and is now fully aware of the size of the task he faces with United entrenched in the relegation zone after 11 matches.

Pochettino attempted to shake things up defensively yesterday with Matthijs de Ligt handed a surprise start, but the Netherlands international, still feeling his way back from a long-term injury, was given the run around by Liverpool’s spritely attack.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, was sent-off after just eight minutes and the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot also hardly covered themselves in glory in the face of relentless pressure from Andoni Iraola’s side.

Despite the obvious defensive issues, the other end of the pitch represents equal concern for Pochettino.

United opted against signing a fresh forward in the summer window, a decision that has spectacularly backfired given the setbacks encountered by Benjamin Sesko.

The Slovenia international displayed signs of promise after a difficult start to his United career last season following his £74million move from RB Leipzig.

A nagging shin injury has restricted the 23-year-old to just six appearances so far this term and he is unlikely to return until the New Year at the earliest.

United’s brains trust has just over a month to consider their options when it comes to recruiting a upcoming forward.

Folarin Balogun, the Monaco striker, wants to be reunited with Pochettino, who coached the former Arsenal player during his tenure as USA head coach.

‘I think my point of view was very clear.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.
  • Industry observers note that anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence organization, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
  • It has been revealed that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.

Industry observers note that anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence organization, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. With a staggering valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, the firm, based in San Francisco, California, is now among the world’s most valuable companies — and it has major ambitions in science.

It has been revealed that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI. Its models have proven powerful in research, and Anthropic has introduced its own directed science effort, focusing on areas including quantum mechanics and protein design. This year alone, it has reported mathematics breakthroughs and launched its first life sciences laboratory.

The IPO might also unleash a historic wave of philanthropy: all seven of Anthropic’s founders are likely to become billionaires and have pledged to donate 80% of their equity in the company to charity, including chief executive Dario Amodei. And on 18 October, the company announced that it had established the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, created to support initiatives that benefit society and stocked with an initial commitment of 5% of Anthropic’s shares.

But the firm has drawn criticism from researchers, who say its aims of curing diseases on short timescales are unrealistic and that its race towards developing ultra-powerful, ‘superintelligent’ AI models pose serious risks, including an existential threat to humanity. In its public prospectus, published ahead of the IPO, Anthropic outlines a newly introduced governance structure that it states is “consistent with our commitment to AI safety and responsibility”, and adds that safety research directly shapes the firm’s “model design, training, and deployment.”.

Nature looks at four areas of science where Anthropic is making waves.

Industry observers note that AI’s potential to turbocharge the discovery of new medicines has been a centerpiece of Anthropic’s pitch to investors. “If today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” Amodei said in a promotional video ahead of the IPO.

The tech giant has been rapidly expanding its biomedical ambitions. This year, Anthropic opened its first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research, announced partnerships with several pharmaceutical companies, and remarked it was pursuing drug leads of its own. “We plan to scale this work up substantially from here,” the company said on 27 October.

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

But Amodei’s habit of promising swift, AI-fueled cures for complex diseases has rankled many researchers and entrepreneurs in the field who feel the timeline is unrealistic.

Recent findings suggest that over the last year, Anthropic has made a major push in the life sciences. In June, the company hired John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize for his work on AlphaFold2 while at Google DeepMind in London.

Some of the company’s early biological research received a mixed reception from biologists. After Anthropic reported using a swarm of AI agents to find signs of a new CRISPR-like system in viral sequence data, some researchers questioned the novelty of the finding and noted that the company had not carried out the experimental work needed to determine the system’s function.

Sources indicate that in protein design — a field that has boomed thanks to specialist AI tools including AlphaFold — Anthropic’s work has also failed to generate much excitement. In August, Anthropic used Claude Science — an agentic system that can access other biological tools and databases — to make novel ‘binders’ against 15 protein targets.

According to recent reports, “Expectations are sky high,” says Anthony Gitter, a computational biologist at the Morgridge Institute for Research in Madison, Wisconsin. “I understand why some view their initial public results as underwhelming.”.

Recent findings suggest that but Gitter is enthusiastic about Anthropic’s protein design efforts, largely because the company was transparent about the work, from the prompts it used to the sequences that were generated. “I would strongly encourage Anthropic to continue that in their future life sciences research,” Gitter adds.

In recent months, Anthropic and other companies — notably Google DeepMind and OpenAI — have been working to establish their research credentials in large part by showing off the rapidly growing mathematical abilities of their flagship AI models.

It has been revealed that on 7 September Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and collaborator Tristan Buckmaster at New York University solved a special case of the Navier-Stokes equations, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics that describes the flow of fluids. Hours after Anthropic announced the result, OpenAI claimed a full solution of the problem, igniting a controversy.

In another collaboration, Alpöge and mathematical physicist Ethan Sussman at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, have been working towards establishing the mathematical foundations of the standard model of particle physics. This too is a problem on which OpenAI has made similar claims.

According to recent reports, anthropic and its competitors see the ability to write a rigorous proof of a mathematical fact as a crucial testing ground for their reasoning models. That’s in large part because the correctness of a proof is an objective measure that can be used as a ‘reward’ to further train AI systems.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

In a recent development, it was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he remarked with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

In a recent development, the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.
