In a recent development, “I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

According to recent reports, “He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Liverpool had already taken the lead when Ronald Araújo rose powerfully to head in a Kostas Tsimikas corner but, two minutes after, the Barcola show began, a confident right-footed shot being swept past Lukas Jungwirth from 10 yards after some good build-up play from Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas.

Industry observers note that it is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

In a recent development, as Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” noted Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are at the moment third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

The Chelsea problem Xabi Alonso cannot ignore - and who is really to blame

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith.

I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

There is no defending Chelsea, because again there was simply no defending by Chelsea.

One goal up and with home advantage against a Leeds team they had already beaten at Stamford Bridge this season in the Carabao Cup, Xabi Alonso and his players took that encouraging platform for success and ripped it up, deservedly losing 4-1.

At least Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United could play the “we only had 10 men” card.

Whatever is failing to function right now at Chelsea is a complex web spun by poor decision-making and performances from a whole host of implicated parties.

The Chelsea defence showcases the Blues’ endemic struggles for consistency in a perfect microcosmic form, not least because there are so many stakeholders who must each accept their share of the blame.

An injury record peculiarly problematic for a team largely only playing once a week this season in the absence of any European football has left them without captain Reece James, summer signing Maxence Lacroix and the improved Jorrel Hato - players whose availability might not cure all their defensive ills, but would certainly help.

Their absences mean more minutes for players not showing any signs that they possess the composure or robustness needed to provide support for a potent attack and secure a return to the Champions League.

Malo Gusto was beaten twice for Brenden Aaronson’s run to goal for Leeds’ fourth - something that happens all too often for a player valued by Chelsea at £75million in the summer transfer market.

Wesley Fofana remains a liability, and his £75m transfer fee back in 2022 - £89.2m adjusted for inflation - surely makes him the worst pound-for-pound signing Chelsea have made in the BlueCo era.

And while Josh Acheampong, 20, has been the one Chelsea defender to draw consistent praise in the first three months of the campaign, he was suspect against Leeds.

So too was Levi Colwill, a player with enormous potential but who has so far failed to rediscover his physicality and form since the torn anterior cruciate ligament that kept him sidelined for almost all of last season.

A question it is worth Alonso and his coaching staff asking themselves: is 34-year-old Emi Martinez clearly a better goalkeeper than Mike Penders, the inevitable long-term No1?

Upcoming details emerge as Chelsea star ‘robbed’ after Leeds game.

Transfer news LIVE: Shock Arsenal move; Man Utd striker deal.

Chelsea get upcoming Rogers penalty review after Leeds handball controversy.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

In a recent development, there is a case to be made to fully blood Penders now, whatever promises might have been made to Martinez when he joined. The Argentine currently looks a shadow of the commanding player he was at Aston Villa.

Wesley Fofana must surely be Chelsea’s worst pound-for-pound signing in the BlueCo era.

Individual errors from Fofana and Gusto and the softness of Colwill and Martinez mean plenty of the blame is rightly being portioned in their direction, but other parties are just as culpable.

In a recent development, alonso, for example, has flattered to deceive as manager so far, switching between a back three and a back four with the result that his team look capable of playing neither, not both. His Chelsea side have scored a laudable 20 league goals but conceded a lamentable 20 at the other end.

Responsibility also lies at the boardroom door, where questionable recruitment has taken place. Benoit Badiashile and Axel Disasi were not at the standard required and have taken too long to move on (still neither player has permanently left the club).

And while he is far from the complete product, Trevoh Chalobah had been one of the more consistent centre-backs of the Clearlake era yet was moved on to high-flying Como this summer in favour of handing a greater amount of game time to Fofana.

If Chelsea are to get back to the pinnacle of English football, which is where the club sees itself, then recruitment, coaching and player performances must all improve.

Accepting shared responsibility is the first step towards revamping and properly rebuilding a defence that simply isn’t going to deliver Champions League football on current form.

Breaking: Chelsea news: The nine mistakes Xabi Alonso has made as Blues manager

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 12:25.

Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United has strengthened the opinion that Xabi Alonso may not necessarily be the correct fit as Chelsea manager.

Not only has the Spaniard defended the multiple occasions that Chelsea have allowed opponents to have the majority of possession, he was seemingly dismissive to the suggestion from the media that his players lack the physicality to compete against the majority of the teams in the Premier League.

Should Chelsea lose at Nottingham Forest - another team far more physically-imposing than themselves - on Friday night, Alonso's win percentage after 15 matches would be almost identical to that of Liam Rosenior's after 23 games.

While that creates an argument that Chelsea's players are to blame for their fall from grace rather than the Spaniard or Englishman, Alonso is responsible for a number of baffling decisions during his time at Stamford Bridge.

Here, Sports Mole highlights nine mistakes that Alonso has made since he was revealed as the club's new manager in May.

With Valentin Barco announcing that he was leaving Strasbourg on May 19, the deal to take him to fellow BlueCo-owned club Chelsea could have been concluded before Alonso's appointment.

However, for unknown reasons, it was not revealed until August 2, suggesting that there was time for Alonso to veto the transfer.

It has been revealed that at 5ft 7ins and of slender build, Barco is simply not equipped to be a Premier League midfielder. While he may have starred for Strasbourg, the Argentine is not a suitable fit alongside Chelsea's other engine-room options.

He has reached this stage of the season with three starts and four substitute appearances, with just 25 minutes coming since October 10.

Given the amount of game time that Marco Palestra was given during pre-season, it was clear that Alonso viewed the Italian as a first-choice pick at full-back or wing-back.

In a recent development, nevertheless, Alonso got carried away. Palestra racked up 311 minutes across four pre-season friendlies played between August 1 and August 15, and the former Atalanta BC player suffered an injury in the days before the opening Premier League game of the season against Fulham.

That prevented the Serie A defender of the year from making his debut until October 10, effectively having to play catch-up as he attempts to acclimatise to English football.

While the 21-year-old started the recent win over Manchester United, he is yet to convince in his current role.

After an extended season that saw him represent Ecuador at the World Cup on July 1, Moises Caicedo was back playing friendlies for Chelsea in the Middle East by August 5.

The midfielder subsequently started three friendlies across 10 days and, like Palestra, suffered an injury in the build-up to the Fulham game.

Caicedo then lasted just 14 minutes on his return from the substitutes' bench against Brighton & Hove Albion six days later and was not seen again until October 10.

He has suffered with a lingering issue ever since, and the way in which Alonso used players during pre-season deserves more scrutiny than it has done.

Alonso went from naming a stronger team than anticipated against Luton Town in the EFL Cup second round to making many alterations versus Leeds United in round three.

Some of that decision-making was justified, yet Alonso himself has taken responsibility for making what he indicates were too many changes for the latter match.

Chelsea ultimately came from 2-0 down to prevail by a 6-3 scoreline in a crazy game, but withdrawing Estevao Willian after 45 minutes started the ball rolling when it came to the Brazilian's frustration over his game time.

Not only did Jordan Henderson make his first start since the World Cup, with no pre-season, in this match, Alonso partnered the veteran Englishman with Barco, who was making his first Premier League start for Chelsea.

Although Chelsea held Brentford for the first hour and Henderson produced a solid performance on debut, this game exposed that Barco weakens Chelsea's midfield, rather than add any match-winning qualities.

Romeo Lavia also remained an unused substitute in this contest, one which Chelsea lost by a 3-0 scoreline.

While some Chelsea fans had been waiting for Geovany Quenda to be handed his first start for Chelsea, they did not anticipate it coming in a London derby against Tottenham Hotspur.

Furthermore, his selection led to Morgan Rogers taking on the number nine role, rather than Danny Welbeck, in the absence of the injured Joao Pedro.

Chelsea subsequently produced one of their most ineffective performances in the final third this season. That was not necessarily because of Quenda, but more through a lack of a traditional number nine to trouble the Spurs defence.

Two weeks later, Alonso chose the same approach against Sunderland, this time using Pedro Neto down the middle.

This decision was essentially made because Chelsea beat Manchester United in the previous game, yet the Red Devils had been the better team in the first half at Stamford Bridge without scoring their opener.

Although there is an argument that Welbeck has not made the expected impact at Chelsea, the 35-year-old has not been given a chance to build up any rhythm and is immediately benched on the back of an ineffective performance.

Despite Emiliano Martinez being signed from Aston Villa to be Chelsea's number one, the Argentine had hardly been at his best prior to suffering a fractured jaw at Everton on October 17.

Meanwhile, Mike Penders recovered from a mistake on his first Premier League start against Spurs to deliver strong showings versus Liverpool, Manchester United and Sunderland, with the only two goals that he conceded coming from penalties.

Regardless, Martinez was back in the starting lineup against Leeds on Saturday, the 34-year-old conceding four goals and making Chelsea appear more vulnerable in defence than they already were.

Alonso has previously indicated that players will be selected on form, but this was a glaring example of choosing status over performances.

Industry observers note that martinez has now conceded 15 goals in 615 minutes for Chelsea. Penders has shipped seven goals in 555 minutes.

Estevao had already struggled against Leeds earlier this season, so the starlet being drafted back into the Chelsea XI for a second Stamford Bridge game versus the Yorkshire giants felt strange.

Furthermore, his inclusion was ahead of Neto, who is Chelsea's strongest winger when it comes to strength and defending. Alonso has already recognised this by using the Portuguese as a wing-back this season.

Neto being omitted from the first XI for a game against opponents of the profile of Leeds made no sense and was more muddled thinking from Alonso. Chelsea were already 3-1 down before he was introduced as a substitute.

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026.

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was declared as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title.

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched.

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021.

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

  • Niko Kovac was under no illusions about the size of the task awaiting his Borussia Dortmund players ahead of facing Arsenal in the Champions League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Niko Kovac was under no illusions about the size of the task awaiting his Borussia Dortmund players ahead of facing Arsenal in the Champions League.

Dortmund make the trip to the Emirates Stadium fresh from beating Borussia Monchengladbach on Saturday, a result that moved them two points clear at the Bundesliga summit.

BVB have started a Bundesliga season unbeaten in their first 10 matches for only the third time, after 2002-03 and 2018-19, while their 24 points at this stage is just one fewer than their club record (25 points in 2010-11 and 2013-14).

However, they face an Arsenal side six points clear at the top of the Premier League despite Mikel Arteta's side drawing 2-2 with Newcastle United at the weekend.

The Gunners are also unbeaten in their last 19 Champions League games (W14 D5 – excluding penalty shootout defeats).

Should they avoid defeat here, they will be just the third English team to go 20+ games without losing in the European Cup/Champions League, after Manchester United (25 – September 2007–May 2009) and Manchester City (26 – September 2022–October 2024).

Dortmund also have a miserable record in England, losing eight of their last nine Champions League away games when facing off against sides from the Premier League.

It has been revealed that arsenal have won three of their four Champions League home games against Borussia Dortmund (L1). Their only loss was in October 2013, with Robert Lewandowski scoring a late winner for the visitors in a 2-1 victory.

"We are not only playing against the best defence in England and Europe, but also against the reigning English champions, Champions League finalists last season and the current Premier League leaders," Kovac told reporters.

"We're aware how difficult this is going to be. They have a great team and a great coach. But we're also difficult to play against, and we'll have our chances.".

Sources indicate that home of The Arsenal. https://t.co/qefVsPBSej.

— Borussia Dortmund (@BlackYellow) November 23, 2026.

Kovac has been handed a double injury boost ahead of facing Arsenal, with the Dortmund boss revealing both Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka are available.

Guirassy, who is BVB's top scorer in all competitions with eight goals in 14 appearances, sustained a hamstring strain just before the international break, while Chukwuemeka has recovered from a thigh problem.

Recent findings suggest that "They're ready for tomorrow's match," added the BVB boss. "They're available for selection. We'll have to wait and see whether they'll start or come on as the match progresses.".

Kovac was also asked about the array of English talent that have come through Dortmund's ranks, with the likes of Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho enjoying successful spells during their time in Germany.

Frank Lampard and Wayne Bridge for Chelsea in April 2004 (at Highbury) and Harry Kane for Bayern Munich in April 2024 (Emirates Stadium) are the only English players to have scored a Champions League away goal at Arsenal.

Jobe Bellingham and Ethan Nwaneri have both appeared in all four of Dortmund's games in the competition this season, although both are still yet to score.

Nwaneri is cleared to play due to UEFA's rules that allow loan players to play against their parent clubs, with the Arsenal forward yet to register a goal involvement across his 13 appearances in all competitions.

"The Bundesliga is a top league where young talent can come through, especially at Dortmund," Kovac noted. "As a club, we are known for developing younger players.

"The English players are very strong physically, technically at the highest level, but the Premier League is the best league in the world and they need playing time.

"A move to Germany, especially Dortmund, is a very good step.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 12:42.

Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury update on Manchester City’s Matheus Nunes ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.

The 28-year-old was unable to recover in time from an ankle problem to feature in City’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham on Saturday.

Nunes has been absent for four of the Citizens’ last seven games in all tournaments this term, but Maresca confirmed at a pre-match press conference on Monday that the right-back “is back” and ready to face Napoli.

"Matheus is back. Then the only one [out] is still Antoine [Semenyo],” Maresca told reporters. “The rest, we have some doubts in terms of tiredness, amount of games, and we have today's session and then we'll decide.".

In a recent development, pushed for more details on Nunes’s recent injury, Maresca added: "This one has been a little bit his ankle, but now he's fine. It's also normal with the amount of games we have, that's why also sometimes I try to rotate players.

"I've mentioned many times, we need to not think about a sprint, we need to think about a marathon; 65 games. So I would like to use the strongest one every game, but then we destroy them. It's also a matter of trying to manage them the best way.”.

Nunes has established himself as Man City’s first-choice right-back when fit and available, while Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis have also been used on the right side of defence under Maresca and predecessor Pep Guardiola.

Man City’s No.27 has played 10 times across all competitions so far this season, but he has been left out of the matchday squad for five games due to injury or fitness-related issues.

According to recent reports, "Since we started, we've used Rico [Lewis at right-back], but also [Khusanov], who I think he can play there,” Maresca explained. “For sure, it's much better... I'm trying to find the right balance.

According to recent reports, "If you ask me if Khusa is a better right-back or central defender, no doubt: Central defender. I know that. But it's a matter of the game, the players we have available.

"But Matheus [Nunes] has done very good since we started, the games he has played, overall he was very good. Rico has [also] done very good so far.”.

It remains to be seen whether Maresca will throw Nunes straight back into the starting lineup against Napoli, with one eye possibly on Sunday’s important Premier League showdown with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Man City have won three of their first four Champions League games in the League Phase and can strengthen their automatic last-16 qualification hopes with a victory against Napoli, who have lost three of their opening four matches in the competition.

Thibaut Courtois described Jude Bellingham as a "leader" on the pitch for Real Madrid, saying Los Blancos' chances of silverware this season may rest with the midfielder.

Courtois' comments came ahead of Madrid's Champions League clash with PSV on Tuesday, with Jose Mourinho's side winning all four of their games in Europe so far.

Madrid are on a nine-game winning run across all competitions, the latest of which came in dramatic fashion against Celta Vigo at the weekend, with Carlos Espi coming off the bench to save his team once again with an 85th-minute winner.

Bellingham was also on target in what was his 100th LaLiga appearance. He has now scored three goals in his last four games, having failed to net in his previous seven.

Since joining from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, Bellingham has played 182 times for Madrid in all competitions, scoring 60 goals as well as providing 41 assists.

He has six goals and three assists so far in 2026-27, and Courtois believes Bellingham is one of Madrid's most notable players despite only being 23 years of age.

"Jude is a young guy but when you see him, it feels like he's a few years older," Courtois told reporters when asked about Bellingham's most impressive qualities.

According to recent reports, "In the beginning, when you compare him with Arda [Guler], Arda was a quieter kid. With Jude, you already feel like he had a presence, but there isn't much difference in age.

"Jude is someone who really wants to win. That's why on the field he swears a lot! He's really a winner, and when he's not happy, he will make it known.

Industry observers note that "He's also a leader on the field. He's a great player, a great mentality. You need those kinds of people like that in your team that go for everything.

In a recent development, "It seems like he has an engine to play 200 minutes. He keeps on going, running with the ball, it's really hard to dispossess him.

"And on the outside, he just works hard, he goes to the gym. With a good Jude, we play better.".

NEXT MATCH @PSV 24/11 | 21:00 CET https://t.co/LcVCq5uN5v.

In a recent development, — Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadriden) November 22, 2026.

It was confirmed earlier this week that Courtois had agreed to fresh terms in the Spanish capital, signing a fresh deal that will keep him with Madrid until the summer of 2028.

"I'm very proud and happy," Courtois noted. "My objective is to end my career here. I want to keep playing and stay healthy. I'm grateful for the club's confidence in me.".

And Courtois will be hoping to play his part against PSV in the Champions League, with this the first meeting between the two sides in 37 years.

According to recent reports, under Mourinho, Real have won 17 of their 20 Champions League matches at the Estadio Bernabeu (D2 L1), with their only defeat coming against Barcelona in the 2010-11 semi-final first leg. It's the best home win percentage (85%) for a manager at a club (min. 20 games) in Champions League history.

"We've had to find how the boss wanted to play, to understand each other better," Courtois mentioned of Mourinho's start to life back in Madrid.

"Our two defeats, against [Real] Betis we didn't deserve to lose, against Atletico [Madrid] the circumstances that led to that result.

"I knew [Mourinho] when I was 22, that was a long time ago. He has a lot more experience. Over the years you change a bit.

According to recent reports, "He's calm, and when he has to speak clearly he speaks clearly. He's a great boss. As a team, we want to keep winning and lift trophies at the end of the season.".

Arsenal have a nervous wait to discover if David Raya is set for a spell on the sidelines.

With talisman Bukayo Saka potentially out for the remainder of the year, Mikel Arteta’s worst-case scenario will be to also lose his starting goalkeeper.

In better news, William Saliba is expected to feature against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday, ahead of the visit of Manchester City at the weekend.

With that in mind, here is the latest Arsenal injury news and return dates….

David Raya has undergone scans on a potential shoulder injury suffered during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Newcastle on Saturday night.

In a recent development, the goalkeeper collided with William Osula while attempting to distribute the ball in the second half and appeared to be in considerable pain as medical staff treated his shoulder. He was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga as the Gunners fought back to claim a point at St James’ Park.

Asked about the goalkeeper after the game, Mikel Arteta told reporters: “Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. He will have an MRI assessment [on Sunday], but at the moment I don't know.”.

He added: “It was a knock, I don’t know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment. We have to wait and see. We know how crucial David is for us. We will have more news [on Sunday].”.

Potential return date: Sunday November 29, vs Manchester City (H).

Martin Zubimendi has endured a frustrating season and has suffered another injury setback after being forced off during Spain's match against England during the international break.

The midfielder has dropped from being Declan Rice's preferred partner to further down the pecking order at Arsenal, with his opportunities limited even before the latest setback. Zubimendi has also been playing with a protective mask after breaking his nose against Everton nearly a month ago.

Spain manager Luis de la Fuente confirmed the Arsenal midfielder had suffered a muscle injury against England, and Mikel Arteta expects him to be sidelined for “a few weeks.”.

”Unfortunately he has a slight problem in his hamstring,” Arteta told reporters on Friday.

"He wasn't too concerned to be fair after the game, but after the MRI scans, it revealed that there is an injury there and he's going to be out for a few weeks.".

Potential return date: Late December.

The initial prognosis was an eight-week absence, which Mikel Arteta believes remains the case after further scans.

The Arsenal manager told reporters last week: "We had another test, he's evolving really well, but it looks like it's going to be an eight-week injury more or less.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 12:44.

Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee could reportedly become the first player to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

The Dutchman joined the Red Devils from Bologna in the summer of 2024 and has since made 86 appearances for the club across all competitions.

Zirkzee has managed just 11 goals and four assists for Man Utd and was heavily linked with a move away from the club during the summer transfer window.

Several Serie A clubs were keen to sign him, with Fiorentina reportedly agreeing a loan fee for the striker, but the proposed move ultimately failed to materialise.

Premier League rivals Everton also made a late push for the 25-year-old, but Man Utd were unwilling to let him leave without first securing a replacement.

Former Man Utd manager Michael Carrick even suggested that Zirkzee could become an important player for the club, but the striker has since slipped considerably down the pecking order.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (via Manchester Evening News), Zirkzee is expected to become the first player to depart in January, with several Italian clubs competing for his signature.

Juventus and Fiorentina are reportedly keen to sign the striker, while Napoli could also enter the race.

The former Bayern Munich attacker has made just seven substitute appearances in the Premier League this season, accumulating 134 minutes of action and scoring once.

Zirkzee has also featured three times as a substitute in the Champions League, where he has registered another goal.

Mauricio Pochettino introduced him in the second half of Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, and the Dutchman managed to make a positive impression despite the disappointing result.

Towards the end of the contest, Zirkzee produced a brilliant pass to Bruno Fernandes, but the United captain's effort was comfortably saved by Alisson Becker.

If Zirkzee fails to earn more opportunities under Pochettino over the coming month, the likelihood of him leaving Old Trafford could increase considerably.

Liverpool have lost a number of their key players on free transfers over the last three years.

Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ibrahima Konate, Mohamed Salah and Roberto Firmino are just some of the players to have left Anfield at the end of their contracts in recent seasons.

The club have become accustomed to letting some of their best players run their contracts down, and it has cost them in the past.

Now, several of Andoni Iraola's key players are entering the final six months of their contracts, and negotiations can soon begin with potential suitors.

One of Liverpool's out-of-contract stars is attracting plenty of interest, and the Reds really could lose him for nothing.

Virgil van Dijk has been absolutely key to Iraola's defence so far this season and is still one of the best performing defenders in the Premier League.

The Dutchman will soon enter the final six months of his deal however, and will then be free to negotiate with clubs from abroad over a free transfer in the summer.

Juventus and AC Milan are the two clubs reported leading the way for the colossus, with the pair keeping a close eye on his contract situation.

That's according to an update from Ekrem Konur, who claims that Italy's two most decorated clubs are ready to battle for Van Dijk's signature.

Conversations over an extension at Anfield are reportedly ongoing, but are yet to bare any fruit, and the future of the Dutchman still remains very uncertain.

Liverpool's recruitment plans seem to hinge heavily on whether or not the skipper puts pen to paper on a new deal, but the partnership formed between Jeremy Jacquet and Van Dijk is something that the Reds won't want to lose.

It isn't yet clear where Van Dijk's preferences lie if a new deal cannot be agreed, but as January edges closer it feels more and more likely that the defender could be playing his final season in Merseyside.

Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have announced they're expecting their first child together.

The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself.

They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino.

The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours.

It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news.

It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece.

Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby.

Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift'.

Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000.

According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano.

There, McTominay can be by the seaside rapidly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre.

The couple regularly share photos from their new life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in substantial moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

Industry observers note that this season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday.

McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test.

The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino.

He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights.

The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly.

'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'.

  • According to recent reports, real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with important issues for Jose Mourinho to manage.
  • Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 13:19.

According to recent reports, real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with important issues for Jose Mourinho to manage. Saturday's 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo was another example of the team's ability to react, but it also exposed problems that the manager cannot ignore.

Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match. The Brazilian, who had served a four-match suspension in La Liga, has regained prominence and has already had his place in the starting line-up for the European tie confirmed by Mourinho. At the same time, the Spanish centre-forward again showed that he can be decisive even with few minutes on the pitch.

According to recent reports, the challenge is to find room for so many options without compromising the collective structure. Real Madrid have Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius, Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler, Yan Diomande and Espi, as well as names who could come into the mix, such as Endrick and Bernardo Silva, but they cannot simply put them all on the pitch and hope that individual talent solves everything.

Vinicius's display against Celta was a reminder of what the Brazilian offers Real Madrid. Coming on 12 minutes into the second half, he gave the attack depth and was able to unbalance defenders in one-on-one situations. For the equaliser, he started the move that ended with Bellingham. For the winner, he crossed for Espi to pounce on the rebound.

Mourinho confirmed that the Brazilian will start against PSV, ending the debate about his status in the team. Peter Bosz's side are known for high pressing, aggressive defending and their attempts to win the ball back quickly. When that first press is beaten, however, they tend to offer space behind the defenders.

That is precisely where Vinicius can be decisive. With his acceleration and ability to attack the space in behind, the Brazilian is a constant threat to a defence that often plays a high line and takes on individual duels all over the pitch. Mbappe can also exploit these spaces.

The question for Mourinho is how to make this threat work without leaving the midfield exposed. Real Madrid cannot rely solely on winning the ball back and launching it to the forwards. They need players close by to connect transitions and sustain possession when necessary.

The presence of Bellingham and Guler between the lines could be key. The Englishman offers ball-carrying and arrivals into the box, while the Turkey international has the quality to find passes that speed up the attack. But the team needs a solid base behind them. Without that, the freedom of the attacking players could prove costly.

It has been revealed that espi's situation is another dilemma. The 21-year-old forward scored the winner against Celta and has three goals in only 44 minutes played in La Liga this season. It is impressive efficiency, but it does not necessarily mean that he should start.

According to recent reports, mourinho was clear in explaining the Spaniard's characteristics. Espi is a penalty-box centre-forward, strong in the air, able to play with his back to goal and to attack the spaces close to the six-yard box. He is not, however, a forward with great mobility to take part constantly in build-up play. The manager also said that the squad does not have the right characteristics to play a pure 4-4-2 with Mbappe and Espi together.

Sources indicate that mbappe likes to start from the left or occupy the space between the full-back and the centre-back, but he is not a traditional winger who tracks the opposition full-back back into his own half. Vinicius also needs freedom to receive the ball wide and accelerate. Putting Espi alongside the Frenchman would require the two wide players to tuck in more and help form a four-man midfield line.

It has been revealed that there are alternatives, but all involve compromises. Bellingham could play deeper, for example. The problem is that Real Madrid would lose part of the Englishman's ability to arrive in the box and would need a midfielder with greater defensive responsibility to compensate. It would also be possible to use Espi in matches where the opposition sit deep and offer less space for the runs of Vinicius and Mbappe.

In a recent development, against tired defences and crosses, Espi offers something different from the other forwards in the squad. His efficiency as a substitute should not be confused with an obligation to change the whole structure of the team.

Recent findings suggest that the win over Celta also left a warning. After turning the scoreline around, Real Madrid finished the game with four forwards on the pitch, as well as Bellingham and Guler in midfield. Mourinho admitted that the team became unbalanced and that he would have liked an extra substitution to bring on Tchouameni and restore defensive protection.

Under Bosz, PSV rely on high pressing, dominating possession, constant movement and a defence that often takes on individual duels. The full-backs can advance into midfield and the forwards take part in the press. It is an aggressive model, capable of suffocating opponents, but one that also leaves space when the first line is beaten.

The impact of each at Real Madrid in 2026-27.

Industry observers note that direct involvements = goals + assists. In the Champions League, Vinicius played four games without a goal or an assist; Espi scored one goal in four games, against Roma. Points gained assume that, without Espi's goals, the three games would have ended in draws. Data up to 21 November 2026.

Sources: FotMob (Opta data), AS and TheStatsAPI.

It has been revealed that real Madrid have the tools to exploit these gaps. Vinicius and Mbappe can attack the space in behind, while Bellingham and Guler have the ability to receive between the lines and speed up the transition. The difficulty will be doing so without turning the game into a series of attacks and counter-attacks.

Industry observers note that real Madrid won their first four league-phase games in the Champions League and are second, with 12 points. The positive run brings calm, but it does not remove the need to improve the collective performance.

It has been revealed that mourinho already has an answer to one of the questions: Vinicius will start. He also knows what Espi can offer and why he does not intend simply to put him alongside Mbappe. The bigger challenge is to make Real Madrid take advantage of the quality of their attackers without losing control of midfield.

Jamie Carragher believes that Manchester United face a fight to stay in the Premier League.

The Red Devils remain mired in the top flight’s relegation zone after their heavy 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday, which saw a nightmare debut for new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

The Argentine, who began work at Carrington last Wednesday, watched on in horror as his new side were outplayed from the off at Anfield, with Leny Yoro sent off inside eight minutes for hauling down Alexander Isak, who was clean through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz got the goals to round off the rout on Merseyside, and it leaves United with just one win in 12 matches in all competitions.

On Sky Sports, Carragher said: “They’re in a relegation fight right now because of where they are in the table. You can’t say anything else when you look at their record this season.

In a recent development, “If the name wasn’t Manchester United and you’re watching the performances, you’d say that is a team that’s in a relegation fight. They’re conceding lots of goals, comedy of errors, red cards, they’ve won one game all season – that is a team in a relegation fight.

Recent findings suggest that “We don’t believe it will happen over a 38-game season but they haven’t had the most difficult of starts. They’ve played a lot of promoted teams, they haven’t played the best team in the league Arsenal yet.

“I don’t think they’ll go down, but this idea that they haven’t got a scrap on their hands- they have.”.

Bruce Arena insisted the San Jose Earthquakes must use the PayPal Park atmosphere to their advantage in their MLS Cup Playoff opener against the Houston Dynamo.

San Jose are back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023 after a strong regular season that saw them finish fourth in the Western Conference, one point clear of Houston.

The Earthquakes have won just one of their last seven MLS games (D4 L2) and enter the postseason on the back of a 3-1 loss to Minnesota United.

Recent findings suggest that and their record on home soil has not been the best in 2026. San Jose won just seven matches in front of their own supporters in the league, the fifth-lowest tally in the West.

Arena, however, believes the San Jose supporters have a substantial role to play when Houston visit for Game 1 of their best-of-three series.

"Making the playoffs was our goal, and we achieved that," remarked Arena. "Now it's going to be key to get a big crowd for the first game against Houston.

"Home-field advantage means something, so if we can get the support from the stands and play well on the field, hopefully that produces a win.".

Industry observers note that but when it comes to the playoffs, the Dynamo have great pedigree. Only three teams have won back-to-back MLS Cup titles, including the 2006-07 Houston side.

The Dynamo also reached the MLS Cup final in 2011 and 2012, but were beaten by the LA Galaxy on both occasions, with the team out for revenge 15 years later.

They have already won the 2023 U.S. Open Cup under head coach Ben Olsen, and now could tie the Columbus Crew (three) for the third-most titles in league history.

Industry observers note that it is the first time since 2023 that San Jose have qualified for the playoffs. They have advanced past Round One only once since returning to the MLS in 2008, knocking out Newly introduced York Red Bulls in 2010.

Houston, meanwhile, are making their first appearance in the playoffs since 2024, coming in with a record of W18 D11 L11 in the postseason.

Their last playoff win came against Sporting Kansas City in 2023, and they have since managed a record of W0 D2 L1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the last couple of years, Liverpool have had a lot of work that they've needed to do on their squad.

Well over £600 million has been spent on new players by them so far and, right now, it's still unclear whether they're actually any better off than they were when Jurgen Klopp was in charge.

Obviously, some arrivals such as Ronald Araujo have been a major upgrade on Jeremie Frimpong but, for others such as Bradley Barcola, some questions still remain.

However, with a lot of Liverpool's focus during the last summer window going on their attack and defence, it feels like the club should now be spending most of their time trying to improve their midfield.

Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai may have been handed new long-term deals last season but, thanks to the way Andoni Iraola uses his midfielders, neither of them have really met expectations.

So, it will hardly come as a surprise to see newly introduced midfielders already being linked with Liverpool.

Liverpool could make a surprise move for Leeds United midfielder Ao Tanaka.

Right now, one of Liverpool's biggest problem areas is their midfield.

As mentioned, a couple of Iraola's current options just aren't cut out for the double pivot role that he wants his midfielders to play.

However, since they didn't sign any new central midfielders in the summer, it feels like that could be their next port of call in January.

Many major-name players have been linked with an Anfield switch but, a surprise option has just emerged.

Ao Tanaka is at the moment plying his trade for Leeds United.

And, even though he was signed by them back when they were in the Championship, he's quickly managed to adjust to life as a Premier League player.

This season alone, the number six has featured in 12 games across all competitions for the West Yorkshire outfit and, according to TEAMtalk, thanks to the fact that his contract expires in 2028, Liverpool have thrown their hat into the ring.

The Japanese international is 28 years old with this deal feeling eerily similar to the one that Klopp struck with VfB Stuttgart for Wataru Endo a few years ago.

Tanaka has plenty of Premier League experience under his belt and, for the right price, he could be a solid signing for Liverpool.

Ao Tanaka would be a very out there signing for Liverpool.

A new number six should be high on Liverpool's priority list.

Without a newly introduced one being brought in, the Reds are going to fall even further behind their title rivals than they right now are.

Indeed, other areas of their squad also need upgrading but, without a newly introduced defensive midfielder being brought in, they're always going to be on the backfoot.

Because, even though Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni are both playing well in their defensive midfield roles, if one of them ends up injured, the Reds are done.

Iraola knows this and by now, you'd hope that Julian Ward does too.

Of course, January is a notoriously hard time to strike deals for players with their prices often being inflated but, in the grand scheme of things, signing someone such as Tanaka, even just as a back-up makes an awful lot of sense.

He'd probably be available for a cut-rate deal and, since he's now 28 years old, this could be his last chance to make a significant move.

Goncalo Ramos got back on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s major win against Frosinone on Sunday evening, expressing his delight after the game.

The pressure has certainly been mounting on Ramos in the last few months. The high price tag paid in the summer came with certain expectations from the Milan fans and with just three goals to his name prior to today’s game, it’s easy to see why there was criticism.

As such, the Rossoneri will be hoping that the goal scored against Frosinone can be a turning point for the No.9. It wasn’t just that he scored the goal either; he got stuck in and played a part in the other goals as well, which we highlighted in the player ratings.

Speaking to Sky and DAZN after the game, as transcribed by MilanNews, Ramos shared his thoughts on the goal and also remarked that Milan are ‘building something beautiful’.

Did you miss the feeling of scoring?

“I’m really happy to have scored. The most important thing is that we won and we played a good team game. The three points are always the most important thing.”.

Sources indicate that “Yes, everything is going very well here: the team, the spirit, the atmosphere. We’re getting to know each other better every day, every week, after every training session, and I think everyone can see it on the pitch like today.

“We’re building something beautiful, and we want to keep working and keep moving forward.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 13:30, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 13:32.

Barcelona will aim to make it five straight wins in all competitions when they continue their Champions League campaign away to Sabah on Wednesday night.

History will be made in this contest, as the two teams prepare to lock horns for the first time, and it would be one of the biggest shocks in Champions League history should Sabah manage to overcome the La Liga champions.

Sabah boast a record of one win and three draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League league stage, which has left them in 31st spot in the table on three points, one point behind 24th-placed PSV Eindhoven.

The Owls opened their league stage campaign with a 4-0 loss to Manchester United, before managing to record a 2-0 victory over Slavia Prague in their second fixture to put three points on the board, but they have since lost to Borussia Dortmund and Viking FC.

Valdas Dambrauskas' side will enter this match off the back of a huge domestic win, beating Sumqayit 5-1, with the result leaving them third in Azerbaijan's top flight, picking up 24 points from their opening 11 games of the season.

Including qualification matches, Sabah have a record of seven wins and five losses in this season's Champions League, keeping five clean sheets in the process.

The Owls had never played in the European Cup before this season, so it is a historic campaign for the club, and they will take on Villarreal, Napoli and Arsenal in their three Champions League league stage fixtures after this one.

As for Barcelona, the Catalan side are currently fifth in the league stage table, picking up nine points from their four matches courtesy of a record of three wins and one defeat.

Hansi Flick's side beat Feyenoord and Galatasaray in their opening two league stage fixtures before suffering a 4-2 reverse to Paris Saint-Germain, but they managed to post a 3-0 victory over Aston Villa last time out to get back on track.

Barcelona will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Villarreal, with that result moving them back to the top of the La Liga table, three points ahead of Real Madrid.

The Catalan side lost in the last-16 stage of last season's Champions League to Atletico Madrid, and it remains to be seen whether their defensive unit is strong enough to make a serious challenge for the 2026-27 European Cup.

Barcelona have actually conceded in each of their last 12 away group stage/league stage matches, but they have scored at least twice in 17 of their last 19 group stage/league stage games.

Barcelona Champions League form:.

Barcelona form (all competitions):.

Sabah will be without the services of Aden McCarthy, with the centre-back suspended on Wednesday following his red card in the team's last Champions League match with Viking.

The hosts also need to make a check on the fitness of Veljko Simic, who is struggling with an injury; the attacker has eight goals in 18 appearances this season and his absence would therefore be a major blow for Sabah.

Joy-Lance Mickels has been in impressive form this season, scoring 12 goals in 22 appearances, and the forward is set to start for the home team.

As for Barcelona, Lamine Yamal will not be involved due to a slight ankle problem, with Barcelona not prepared to take any risks when it comes to the Spain international.

Roony Bardghji (knee), Xavi Espart (ankle), Rodri (hamstring) and Andreas Christensen (muscle) are also unavailable for selection.

Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal on Sunday due to an issue that he sustained while on international duty with Spain, but the centre-back was on the bench and should feature in the starting team.

Meanwhile, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi are expected to join Raphinha in the final third of the field due to the absence of Yamal.

Sabah possible starting lineup:.

Pokatilov; Zedadka, Solvet, Almeida, Puchaz; Lepinjica, Isayev, Rakhomaliev; Severina, Mbina, Mickels.

Barcelona possible starting lineup:.

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Fermin, Bernal, Pedri; Adeyemi, Raphinha, Gordon.

Yamal's absence is a major blow for Barcelona, but the Catalan outfit have enough quality in their side to secure all three points on Wednesday.

Paul Merson has questioned Chelsea’s decision to appoint Xabi Alonso in the summer.

The Blues sank to a new low over the weekend when they were thrashed 4-1 by Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

It saw the west Londoners slump to eighth in the Premier League table, five points off the top four.

They have now registered just one win in their last five games as pressure piles on Alonso in his first term in the hotseat.

On Sky Sports, Merson, the former Arsenal striker, disputed the Spaniard’s appointment and rhetorically asked why Liverpool had not hired their former midfielder, despite him being a free agent and Arne Slot being sacked at the end of the season.

"My biggest worry is that Liverpool could have had Alonso and they chose not to,” he said.

“Obviously, Liverpool didn't think he was good enough.

Recent findings suggest that "Alonso took the Chelsea job, and Liverpool sacked Slot two weeks later. You can't tell me that Liverpool couldn't have spoken to Alonso and say: 'Don't take the Chelsea job, we're going to take you'.

Industry observers note that "He was out of a job as well, Liverpool could have had him and he'd have gone there all day long. So why didn't they take him? Did they know something that we're seeing now?

"It just always sits in my mind. That was my worry - and now it's playing out.”.

Merson compared Alonso to his predecessor, Liam Rosenior, who was dismissed after just three months in charge, having lost five consecutive league games without scoring - the club’s first time since 1912.

"If this was Rosenior in charge at Chelsea and getting these results, he'd be in major trouble,” Merson continued.

“100 per cent, he'd be in trouble. And remember, Rosenior didn't have Morgan Rogers in his team, bought for £116million.

"But it's because of the unbelievable job [Alonso] did at Bayer Leverkusen that everybody is thinking: ‘It will be alright.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Keith Andrews said his decision to make several changes to Brentford's starting line-up against Everton on Monday revealed ambition to compete on all fronts this season.
  • Andrews watched on as his Brentford side responded from their 2-0 defeat to Brighton ahead of the international break with a thumping 4-0 triumph over 10-man Everton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Keith Andrews said his decision to make several changes to Brentford's starting line-up against Everton on Monday revealed ambition to compete on all fronts this season.

Andrews watched on as his Brentford side responded from their 2-0 defeat to Brighton ahead of the international break with a thumping 4-0 triumph over 10-man Everton.

Keane Lewis-Potter netted twice in the space of 178 seconds in the first half to put the Bees in control before Everton captain James Tarkowski was sent off in the 40th minute.

Tarkowski was dismissed for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk high on his shin after clearing the ball, with referee Craig Pawson overruling his original decision after a VAR review.

Vitaly Janelt's 67th-minute thunderbolt was the pick of Brentford's goals, with substitute Fabio Carvalho climbing off the bench to add further gloss to the scoreline late on.

Brentford enjoyed their joint-biggest home win in the Premier League, equalling their 4-0 rout of Manchester United in August 2022, with their display coming after Andrews elected to make four changes to the side that were beaten by Brighton.

Callum Wilson replaced the suspended Igor Thiago up front, while Yarmoliuk, Mikkel Damsgaard and Jaidon Anthony all came in to replace Mamadou Sangare and Kevin Schade, while Aaron Hickey missed out all together through injury.

"Big impact, it's the nature of the game and the squad. We have the luxury of choosing from very good players," Andrews told Sky Sports on the reason behind his alterations.

"Some will be disappointed not to play more, but the reality is we need everybody. We want to be ambitious, so we need everybody. The boys that came in did really well.".

— Everton (@Everton) November 23, 2026.

After missing out on European football last season, Brentford's win saw them climb up to sixth in the Premier League and just four points adrift of fourth-place Liverpool.

"We know what the other side feels like, but I wanted to keep our habits, be professional, try to control the game and wait for the right openings," Andrews added.

Sources indicate that "Each game is very different, very difficult. The expectation levels at this club have changed and, regardless of the performance, the win to go sixth in the league and still questions about 'should they be doing better?' – I think people need to get real.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue. Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it.".

Since Andrews took charge of Brentford ahead of the 2025-26 season, of London clubs, only Arsenal (113) have won more Premier League points than the Bees (70).

Brentford also hit the 300-goal mark in the Premier League in their 201st game in the competition (303 goals in total), the fifth-fastest side to do so, after Man United (165), Newcastle United (170), Liverpool (190) and Blackburn Rovers (191).

Lewis-Potter got the landmark goal, and in 11 appearances this season, he has already beaten his best-ever scoring season in the Premier League (three in 36 apps in 2025-26 and 3 in 30 in 2023-24), with his double taking him to four this term.

"He's been excellent, growing all the time since I've been here," Andrews remarked of Lewis-Potter.

"Finds himself in unnatural positions – we give him the freedom to go and roam, and he's proving very difficult for the opposition to mark.".

  • Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.
  • Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:32.

Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.

Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.

The England international has gradually slipped down the pecking order at the Santiago Bernabeu under Jose Mourinho, with Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries seemingly ahead of him.

Alexander-Arnold was also subjected to boos from sections of the home support following his lacklustre performance in Real Madrid's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo last week.

Former Liverpool and England striker Emile Heskey recently suggested that Alexander-Arnold should consider a move to Bayern, although he admitted he would love to see the defender return to Anfield.

However, Bild journalist Christian Falk has categorically dismissed the links, suggesting that Bayern are more interested in signing players such as Givairo Read than Alexander-Arnold.

Bayern already have Konrad Laimer and Josip Stanisic available for the right-back position, while Sacha Boey also remains at the club.

Even if Vincent Kompany decides to make changes in that department, he would reportedly favour a younger profile, meaning Alexander-Arnold is unlikely to be a genuine option for the German champions.

Speaking to CFBayern Insider, Falk said: "It is not true - Bayern Munich are interested in Real Madrid fullback Trent Alexander-Arnold. Bayern are searching for a player in this position, and players like Givairo Read are definitely still of interest.

"You can tell from Read’s profile alone that the club just isn’t looking to add a player like Alexander-Arnold to the ranks. Also, I’m not sure if Vincent Kompany would look at the Englishman’s profile, as he’s not a typical right-back for Bayern Munich.

Sources indicate that "He’s also not the youngest footballer any more. And, if we’re being honest, the 28-year-old hasn’t proven himself at Real Madrid.

"You have to have a lot of respect for English players who give it a go playing in another country. But not every English player succeeds after leaving the UK, and not every English player is Harry Kane! So, I don’t think Alexander-Arnold will be a genuine option for Bayern in the summer.".

While an emotional return to Anfield would appeal to many supporters, the reality is that Liverpool have probably moved on, even though the right-back position remains a somewhat problematic area for them.

Jeremie Frimpong has yet to convince everyone, while there is also uncertainty over whether the Reds will sign Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a permanent deal.

With Conor Bradley's injury record remaining a concern and Joe Gomez potentially departing next summer, Andoni Iraola could look to bring in a fresh right-back, although it remains doubtful whether Liverpool would consider a move for their former player.

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that it was crucial that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team showed the levels that they are capable of.

Now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

“It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

“Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it showed towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

In a recent development, “We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”.

Sources indicate that are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

Recent findings suggest that “We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

It has been revealed that “I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”.

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

It has been revealed that “I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”.

What will you say ahead of Olympiacos?

According to recent reports, “The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

“But that’s not an excuse. I noted the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

According to recent reports, “Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

“Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an crucial objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”.

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

“I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

According to recent reports, “Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”.

Mikel Arteta has warned Ethan Nwaneri that "moments are not enough" if he is to turn his Borussia Dortmund loan around.

The young forward joined the German club in the summer on loan from Arsenal and he was initially handed opportunities in the starting lineup by Niko Kovac.

It has been revealed that however, those have been few and far between in recent weeks. Nwaneri has not started a match in over a month and has played just five minutes of football across Dortmund's last three league matches.

The German side, who sit top of the Bundesliga, travel to north London to take on the Premier League champions on Tuesday in the Champions League and Nwaneri is eligible to face his parent club.

It appears unlikely, though, that the 19-year-old will start against the Gunners considering Dortmund's fine form, and Arteta has warned the teenager that nothing will come easy.

"We're talking here about the highest level in Europe," Arteta remarked.

"To play at that level is extremely difficult. You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a significant amount of minutes and have a huge impact at such big football clubs like Arsenal and Dortmund is extremely difficult.

According to recent reports, "That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency.

"Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that but it takes some time.".

Arteta added: "He needs to earn the right to play. He's playing at the top of the Bundesliga and the players have huge talent and quality and they are showing that and that's the reality of football.

"You go there and because you come from Arsenal, it doesn't give you any advantage, so you need to earn it.

"Ethan has, first of all, the mindset to do it and then the quality to do it and these things are part of a journey and part of a season and he needs to reveal himself and earn the right to win.".

Nwaneri spent the second half of last season on loan at Marseille and barely played after Roberto De Zerbi's departure in February.

Arsenal are understood to have the option to recall Nwaneri in January if his loan at Dortmund is proving to be similarly unproductive.

"In Marseille he had a completely different context for a lot of things that are so unexpected to happen.

"But that builds a player and builds the character. I'm so convinced of that. You are about to fulfil a role that you are given on the day and try and change that for the one you actually want. That's football.".
